about: WebUI design review records (docs/working/WEBUI_UX_REVIEW_2026-10-25.md): the three page audits in full, and each research pass's principles and implementation references; the sources are in .claude/skills/webui-design/references/sources.md.

findings.title: An uncalibrated score is labelled 'Confidence', and the scores appear twice for the selected candidate
findings.evidence: diagnosis_panel.py:1313-1315 sets the table header to 'Rank | Disease | Confidence | GNN | SP | Evidence'. details_header_html (1359-1363) then repeats 'Confidence 0.xxx · GNN 0.xxx · SP 0.xxx' under '#rank name', while the same table row stays visible beside it. The Evidence column's coloured dots use raw hex outside the tokens (2444-2447: #1f9d55, #d69e00 at 2.4:1, #3b6fe0). The table has 6 columns and still no phenotype match count.
findings.fix: 1) Rename the column to 'Score' and give it an ⓘ (plain text is fine for this): 'Relative to the other candidates in this list. Not a probability that the patient has the disease.' Ref: the Isabel Pro likelihood-bar disclaimer. 2) Use the columns Rank | Disease | Score | Phenotypes k/N | Evidence. Render the score as right-aligned 3 decimals with tabular-nums, plus a CSS bar scaled to the list maximum: (ref: the LIRICAL 'Top Differential Diagnoses' table). Compute k/N in the renderer from _query_phenotypes and matching_phenotypes, with no API change. 3) Show GNN and SP only in the details Evidence key-value list, and cut details_header_html down to '#rank name ID'. 4) Move the dot colours onto --shep-status-* tokens. 5) Add a renderer test that each candidate's score string occurs once outside the drawer and the exports.

findings.page: Shell (global theme tokens), affects Diagnosis, Settings and Training
findings.title: Placeholders and info= text, including a refusal, still use Gradio's subdued grey at 2.54:1
findings.evidence: The Soft theme leaves body_text_color_subdued = neutral_400 (#9ca3af). block_info_text_color and input_placeholder_color inherit it (.venv gradio/themes/base.py:1149, 1201-1202, 1669-1670). style.py:209-214 overrides the label and checkbox colours but not these, and nothing in src/webui sets --block-info-text-color. Result, at 2.54:1 on white: the HPO format placeholder 'HP:0001250 — Seizure … (commas / spaces are fine too)' and 'Patient ID (auto-generated if blank)' (01-diagnosis-empty.png; diagnosis_panel.py:1990-1994), and the state-bearing refusal training_console.py:2815 gr.update(info=AMP_HGT_REFUSAL). The help.py docstring (lines 19-22) names that refusal as text that must stay visible.
findings.fix: Add to the token block in style.py: .gradio-container { --block-info-text-color: var(--shep-text-2); --block-info-text-size: 14px; --input-placeholder-color: #6b7280; } (#434a58 is 8.9:1 and #6b7280 is about 4.8:1 on white). Do this before moving any must-know line into info= (P06). Add a contrast test that reads these computed colours in the existing probe.

findings.title: The PREPARE/EVALUATE group labels sit in the tab row and read as two more tabs
findings.evidence: Every Research screenshot shows 'PREPARE  Datasets  Training  |  EVALUATE  Test  Models' on one 44px line. The labels are centred on the tabs' baseline (style.py:146-150: top:0; bottom:0; align-items:center) at 14px/600 uppercase with .07em spacing in #5b6270. The tabs are 15px/500 in #434a58, so in 04-datasets.png 'PREPARE' looks as heavy as 'Datasets'. The gap from 'PREPARE' to 'Datasets' is about 19px (right: calc(100% + 6px) plus 12px of tab padding), against about 24px between two tabs, so proximity reads them as one sequence. Only EVALUATE has a divider (style.py:153); PREPARE has none. The offsets are hard-coded to font metrics (style.py:144-145: margin-left 84px / 116px).
findings.fix: Keep the CSS generated content (content: 'Prepare' / ''), pointer-events:none and RESEARCH_TABLIST_LABEL, and insert no nodes into the tablist. Option A (preferred; the owner must exempt overlines from the 14px floor in the no-text-under-14px test): make the labels overlines. Rules: #shep-research-nav > .tab-wrapper > .tab-container { padding-top: 14px; } and the ::before { top: 2px; bottom: auto; left: 12px; right: auto; display: block; font-size: 12px; line-height: 1; }. Drop the 84px margin and set #shep-page-test-button { margin-left: 24px; border-left: 1px solid var(--shep-border); }. Option B (keeps 14px): keep the labels inline but make them read as labels. Use sentence case with a colon (content: 'Prepare:' / ''), text-transform none, letter-spacing 0, weight 400. Give both groups a 1px x 20px divider and a 24px gap, and size the margins from the new label widths. Either way, add a selector-inventory DOM test for #shep-page-*-button::before under 6.30 and a hover/cursor/Tab-order check (refs: PatternFly grouped navigation, the Windows ribbon group labels, the WAI-ARIA APG Tabs pattern).

findings.title: Help bubbles are long run-on paragraphs with no lead line and no emphasis
findings.evidence: 02-diagnosis-help-bubble.png: the 'Model in use' bubble is 15 lines. CARD_HELP (diagnosis_card.py:107-118) is 123 words in 3 sentences, the longest 49 words. It repeats 'after each diagnosis, after a model change and with ↻' twice and explains polling cadence before the one fact users need, that a grey card shows the last known state, which comes last. Other texts: D8 chip 91 words with one 52-word sentence (chips.py:60-72); dx-badge 77 words; dx-exports one 34-word sentence written 'CSV = … · report = …' (diagnosis_panel.py:1086-1091). In 09-test-help-bubble.png, 'R10 labels' is about 190 words of dot-joined clauses. The renderer cannot emphasise anything: help.py:268 sets bd.textContent = textOf(btn), with white-space: pre-line at :445.
findings.fix:
(a) Renderer: replace help.py:268 with a function of about 30 lines that builds the body only with createElement and textContent. Line 1 becomes

; '- ' lines become

  • ; 'Term: text' becomes Term plus a text node; a blank line starts a new

    . Use white-space:normal inside the li. Never use innerHTML (ref: OWASP DOM XSS cheat sheet, rule 3; VS Code formattedTextRenderer pattern). (b) Rewrite each text as a lead line plus at most 3 bullets, about 60 words or fewer. For example, CARD_HELP: 'The model every session is served now. - Grey card: the last read failed or is older than the result; it shows the last known state. - ↻ reads it again (it also refreshes every 5 s). - Chips mark states that change results: synthetic data, no SP table, unverified.' (c) Add a registry test: ≤80 words, sentence ≤25 words, lead ≤90 characters. Add one test that '' renders as text and one that '- a - b' gives 2

  • .

findings.title: The bubble covers the element it explains and is wider than the budget
findings.evidence: 02-diagnosis-help-bubble.png: the MODEL IN USE bubble opens downward (y 490-908) and hides the card ('No model loade…'), Run Diagnosis and its disabled reason. 09-test-help-bubble.png: the R10 bubble opens upward and hides the Result rows it explains. help.py:243-259 positions against the ⓘ's own rect only (below, else above, left = r.left - 24). Width is capped at 360px (help.py:245, 424), where the budget is 320px.
findings.fix: In place(): find the explained region with var reg = anchor.closest('.shep-dx-card, .shep-panel-hd, .block, tr, .shep-kv') || anchor, and its panel with anchor.closest('.shep-panel'). Try the placements in a fixed order and take the first that fits, as Floating UI's flip() does with fallbackPlacements (port the algorithm in about 25 lines; no library and no CDN). The order: (1) right of the panel, left = panel.right + 12, top clamped to r.top - 12, arrow on the left (.shep-left); (2) left of the panel; (3) below reg.bottom; (4) above reg.top. Cap the width at min(320px, vw - 24). The left 370px Diagnosis column always has room on its right.

findings.title: The environment warning leads with a version list, buries the problem and never states the consequence
findings.evidence: Every screenshot ends with '⚠️ torch 2.10.0+cu130 · CUDA 13.0 (no device) · PyG 2.8.0.post1 · native ext OK · Voyager — torch is built for CUDA 13.0 but no device is visible — check the driver and CUDA libraries'. app.py:82 bolds the 5-item version chain (⚠️ {line}) and leaves the actual problem in plain text at the end. It never says that GPU training and tests are unavailable. The healthy state is #888 on #f3f4f7, 3.22:1 (app.py:84, fails). The notice and degraded colours are raw hex (#b45309, #d32f2f) outside the tokens. The row costs 32px on every page.
findings.fix: Lead with the consequence in one bold line: 'CUDA device not visible: GPU training and GPU tests are unavailable.' Put the versions behind a native <details><summary>Environment details</summary> or an ⓘ topic. Better, render NOTICE/DEGRADED as a third header chip in chips.chips_html (amber or red lozenge, ⚠ icon, text 'Environment: no CUDA device', ⓘ with the package list) and drop the footer row when the environment is healthy; show the healthy version line in Settings. Use --shep-amber-800 (7.1:1) and --shep-red-700 tokens. The per-page refusals (Training Start, Test Start) stay inline next to their controls.

findings.title: The read-only state is quieter than the normal state, and the chips look like buttons
findings.evidence: 01-diagnosis-empty.png: '🔒 Operator controls: on (this machine) ⓘ' is an indigo pill (accent-50 fill, accent text; style.py:72-79, 79). That is the same treatment as the selected Settings tab (style.py:113-115), the field label chips and links. The state viewers must notice, 'Read-only: request not local', is rendered grey (style.py:80, shep-chip-readonly), weaker than the normal 'on'. 'GPU jobs: none' is a bordered pill with a dot, although nothing needs attention. The constant prefix 'Operator controls:' puts the distinguishing word ('on'/'Read-only') at word 3 (chips.py:57).
findings.fix: Use one status vocabulary with --shep-status-{error,serious,warn,ok,info,neutral} tokens, each state shown as icon or shape plus text. Normal states are plain text with no pill border: lock glyph + 'Operator: on' in text-2, and 'GPU: idle' muted. Only states to watch get a lozenge: 'Read-only: <reason>' in amber with the lock, 'GPU: training (job runner)' in info blue with the dot (animate only while running), 'not read' in grey dashed. Leave no hover or pointer on the chip body; the ⓘ stays the only control (ref: Carbon status indicator pattern, Atlassian Lozenge).

findings.title: The Diagnosis/Research switch looks like a selected form radio, and Settings has a fourth navigation look
findings.evidence: 05-training.png: the selected 'Research (pre-clinical)' (accent fill, white, 700; style.py:101-103) is identical to the selected radios 'gat' and 'auto' (Soft checkbox_label_background_fill_selected = primary_500). In 01 the filled switch is the heaviest element on the screen, heavier than the page's primary action. In-page .shep-seg is also a pill segmented control (style.py:163-166). In 12-settings.png, the selected Settings is an accent-50 box with a 3px inset underline (style.py:113-116), so neither stage is selected. Settings is announced as a tab of the 'Stage' tablist (shell.py:432, 492).
findings.fix: Keep the accent fill for primary actions and selected form values. Restyle level 1: selected segment = background var(--shep-grey-800), border var(--shep-grey-800), white text, weight 600 (two cues, distinct from the indigo radios and from the grey-track .shep-seg); unselected = white with a #8d94a1 border (3:1). Style Settings as a link-like right tab: text-2, selected = text colour plus a 3px underline, no box. Rename the tablist aria-label from 'Stage' to 'Main navigation'.

findings.page: Shell (operator controls on Diagnosis, Training, Test, Models)
findings.title: A padlock on enabled buttons carries no state
findings.evidence: Enabled buttons carry the padlock: 01 '🔒 Load a model…' (primary), 03 '🔒 Load this model', 05 '🔒 ▶ Start' and '🔒 Continue...', 09 '🔒 Import a new version…' and '🔒 Register this report'. Disabled buttons beside them carry the same glyph: 09 '🔒 Start test', '🔒 Cancel'. Sources: diagnosis_card.py:631, diagnosis_panel.py:2032. A padlock reads as 'locked/unavailable', and the header already says 'Operator controls: on'.
findings.fix: Add one helper, renderers.gated_label(text, allowed), and use it at every gated button. Allowed: plain label ('Load a model…'). Refused: '🔒 ' + label, disabled, with the visible 'Operator controls only: <reason>' line beside it (D8). change_button() already knows state['operator'].

findings.title: Field labels are indigo chips, and each page mixes 3 or 4 label styles
findings.evidence: 01: 'HPO terms' and 'Patient ID (optional)' are indigo pills (Soft block_title_background_fill = primary_100, soft.py:54-65; style.py:209-211 only recolours the text). Beside them: 'Options' 14px/500 plain, 'Top-K' 15px dark, 'MODEL IN USE' 14px/700 uppercase .08em (diagnosis_panel.py:2384). 05: 'DATASET' and 'RUN NAME' uppercase next to 'Epochs' and 'Learning Rate' chips. 12: 'Memory Allocator' chip. The same indigo pill marks status chips and selected states, so labels read as tags or buttons.
findings.fix: Use one label style site-wide via theme variables in style.py (the names are verified in the 6.30 bundle): .gradio-container { --block-title-background-fill: none; --block-title-padding: 0; --block-title-text-color: var(--shep-text); --block-title-text-weight: 600; }. Replace .shep-dx-card-title and Training's DATASET/RUN NAME uppercase micro-labels with the same 14-15px/600 sentence case ('Model in use', 'Dataset', 'Run name').

findings.page: Diagnosis, Settings (all text inputs and dropdowns)
findings.title: Input boundaries are nearly invisible
findings.evidence: Soft sets input_border_color = neutral_50 (#f9fafb), 1.05:1 on the white panel, with only a 10% drop shadow (soft.py:69-71). In 01, the HPO textarea, Patient ID and Top-K boxes are faint white-on-white shapes, and the 12-settings dropdown is the same. style.py:212 fixed the checkbox border for exactly this reason but left text inputs alone.
findings.fix: .gradio-container { --input-border-color: #8d94a1; --input-border-color-focus: var(--shep-accent); --input-shadow: none; --input-shadow-focus: 0 0 0 2px var(--shep-accent-100); } (#8d94a1 is 3.05:1 on white, the grey the ⓘ already uses).

findings.title: The input format rule is only in a placeholder and a bubble, and the example implies names are read
findings.evidence: Placeholder 'HP:0001250 — Seizure\nHP:0001263, HP:0002376   (commas / spaces are fine too)' (diagnosis_panel.py:1990-1991): grey at 2.54:1, gone once typing starts. The must-know rule 'Names and stray punctuation are ignored; only HP:####### ids are used' lives only in the ⓘ (FIELD_HELP 1053-1055). A user who types 'Seizure' gets nothing on screen saying it will be ignored.
findings.principle: P06, DX-12, P19 (refs: GOV.UK text input 'hint text', NN/g 'Placeholders in Form Fields Are Harmful')
findings.fix: Use gr.Textbox(info='Only HP:####### ids are read; names and punctuation are ignored.'). This needs the --block-info-text-color fix first. Note that 6.30 escapes HTML in info, while **bold** and `code` work. Shorten the placeholder to 'HP:0001250, HP:0001263'. Patient ID: info='Blank: the server assigns an id.' and no placeholder. Keep the ⓘ for the dedupe detail.

findings.title: No echo of which HPO ids were recognised or used
findings.evidence: The input column shows no count or list of the parsed ids before Run. After Run, the results header shows '<n> candidates · <x> ms · produced <time>' (diagnosis_panel.py:1184-1187) but never 'N terms used' or the ids that were dropped. Dedupe is mentioned only inside the ⓘ ('the service removes them and says how many').
findings.fix: Under the textarea, add a plain_html line updated on .input (local, no API, show_progress='hidden'). It renders _parse_hpo_ids(text) as '3 ids recognised · not ids: "Seizure"' (escaped). After a run, show one 'As used' chip row at the top of the results: 'Seizure · HP:0001250' with the label from the local ontology (src/ontology/loader.py), and an amber 'Not used (n)' with a reason per id (duplicate, unknown, not in graph) using the API's dedupe count. Ref: the LIRICAL report's input-error list. Add the same split to the CSV and report.

findings.title: 'No model loaded' appears four times and 'no result yet' twice
findings.evidence: 01-diagnosis-empty.txt, card: 'No model loaded' + 'No pipeline is configured on this server; nothing is served.' (diagnosis_card.py:587-589). Run reason: 'Disabled: no model loaded. Load one with “Load a model…” above.' (diagnosis_panel.py:1119). Results: 'Run Diagnosis needs a loaded model. The card on the left says what is loaded.' + 'Each result says what produced it, compared with the model in use.' (1196-1201). Header right 'no result yet' directly over the body title 'No result yet' (1181, 1199).
findings.fix: Make the card the one place that says it: 'No model loaded' plus its one action. Shorten the run reason to 'Disabled until a model is loaded.' (the D8 reason stays visible). For no_model, the results empty state becomes title 'Load a model to start' with no second sentence and no 'Each result says…' note; keep the note only in the ⓘ of the badge. Render nothing at the header's right while there is no result.

findings.title: Evidence uses internal jargon, and phenotypes and paths show bare ids
findings.evidence:
evidence_html uses headings '

Mode A — Direct path evidence

' and 'Mode B — Analogy-based evidence', plus 'Shortest: 2 hops · 4 direct paths' (diagnosis_panel.py:1390-1405). phenotypes_html prints only HP:… (1418). paths_html joins raw node ids with → (1429-1433). The 34-word MATCHING_NOTE (1137-1141) repeats under every list.
findings.fix: 1) Replace the Mode headings with a shep-kv list: 'Evidence type: Direct links in the knowledge graph | Shortest link: 2 steps | Direct paths: 4 | Supporting genes: …' ('Similar genes' for Mode B). Put the narrative in native <details><summary>Full explanation</summary>. 2) Add one term_html(id, label) helper: label first, id in muted mono, labels from the local ontology (HP) and the KG node names (MONDO, genes); 'HP:0001250 (name not in this ontology release)' when the lookup fails. 3) Show Matching phenotypes as 'Annotated to this disease (k)' / 'Not annotated (N-k)', computed from _query_phenotypes, with the note cut to one line. 4) Render paths as typed chip rows ('[Phenotype] … → [Gene] … → [Disease] …'): the 3 shortest, then <details>All n paths</details>, all inside the same gr.HTML, so there is no visible= toggling.

findings.page: Diagnosis, Change model drawer (and Models, Test, Training workspace selects)
findings.title: Option labels and model rows are dot-joined chains that repeat facts
findings.evidence: 03-diagnosis-model-drawer.png. Option: '<b>odd&name · dataset fingerprint 3f563f74bb04 · synthetic', from renderers.workspace_choices (375-392), which every page shares. Run header 'Run gat/20261019-090000_run_<i>x · started 2026-10-19 09:00' sits directly over the row 'GAT · run 2026-10-19 09:00 · epoch 2', so the time and 'gat' appear twice. Row sub-line 'model fingerprint 536d8a31d4f6 · trained on <b>odd&name, demo, m5_webui_demo_01 · dataset fingerprint 3f563f74bb04 · synthetic' repeats the dataset fingerprint and 'synthetic' already shown in the select.
findings.fix: Keep the (label, value) tuples and change only the labels. workspace_choices returns (name, name), or 'name · synthetic' when that is needed to tell entries apart, at most 40 characters. The fingerprint appears once, in the line under the select (Models already renders 'built … dataset fingerprint 3f563f74bb04 [copy]'), or through gr.update(info='dataset `3f563f74bb04`') on .select. Run group header: 'Oct 19 09:00 · GAT'. Row: 'Epoch 2 · val MRR 0.100' plus status tags. Model fingerprint and trained-on move to the facts column as a summary list (ref: GOV.UK summary list; MLflow DetailsOverviewCopyableIdBox for the 12-hex + copy). Add a unit test: label ≤40 characters, at most one ' · ', no 7+ hex run.

findings.title: Two navigation rows plus the footer take 131px of a 964px window
findings.evidence: 04/05/10: header 0-54px, research tab row 55-99px, footer 932-964px. On Training these 131px come out of the chart grid (the owner's 'charts squeezed' complaint). At 1847px, row 1 has about 690px free between the end of the switch (x≈577) and the chips (x≈1270).
findings.fix: (1) Move the footer into a header chip (see the footer finding): saves 32px. (2) When Research is selected and the shell's layout() pass finds room, draw the research tab row inside row 1 to the right of the switch, in the underline style. Implementation: #shep-shell.shep-research-inline #shep-research-nav > .tab-wrapper { position:absolute; top:0; left: var(--shep-tabs-x); height: var(--shep-row1-h); background:none; border:0 }. Measure --shep-tabs-x in layout() the way --shep-settings-w is measured now, and fall back to the current second row when it does not fit (narrow widths, 13-training-narrow-960.png). Group labels then need option A or B of the group-label finding. Pin the internal selectors with the inventory test (G10). Gain: about 45px more chart height.

findings.title: Four sizes and four weights, with 14, 15 and 16px too close to form a hierarchy
findings.evidence: Sizes in style.py: brand 17/700 (:64), panel h2 16/600 (:287), tabs 15/500 with selected 15/700 (:97, 102, 136, 140), body 15, meta 14. Weight 500 also on .shep-dx-opt (diagnosis_panel.py:2369); 700 on .shep-dx-card-title (:2384) and .shep-fpv (style.py:236). Squint test on 01 and 12: panel titles at 16px barely differ from body at 15px, and the strongest block is the filled header switch, not the results panel. Settings' page title 'Runtime Settings' renders the same size as its sections 'Memory' and 'Compute'.
findings.fix: Define tokens --shep-fs-title: 20px (at most 2 per page; on Diagnosis only 'Diagnosis results', on Settings the page title), --shep-fs-body: 15px, --shep-fs-meta: 14px (keeps the owner's floor). Use weights 400 and 600 only. Selected tabs keep 3 cues: colour, the 3px underline and 600. Other panel titles become 15/600. Add a test that greps the head CSS for font-size and font-weight values outside the tokens.

findings.title: A wall of text, actions above the settings they apply, and controls stretched to 1800px
findings.evidence: 12-settings.png. A 60-word intro with 4 bold fragments, plus an italic 'An explicit PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF … overrides …' line shown even when no override is active (runtime_settings.py:220-229). A second warning appears when one is active (233-240), so the fact can show twice. 'Apply Settings' (900px, primary) and 'Restart Backend' (900px) sit above the fields (247-254). The Memory Allocator dropdown spans 1800px for the value 'cuda_async'. There is no shep-panel, unlike every other page.
findings.fix: Wrap the page in a shep-panel with max-width about 760px. Title at 20px. Cut the intro to one line: 'Hardware settings: speed, memory and precision. Model settings are in Research › Training.' Show the env-override sentence only when it is active, as one .shep-notice-amber at the top. Fields first; then an action row in the panel footer (shep-panel-ft) with a normal-size 'Apply settings' primary button and the 'Applied: …' status beside it. Restart moves next to the allocator (next finding).

findings.title: Restart backend is one click for every session, and the page never shows whether a restart is pending
findings.evidence: restart_btn.click → _on_restart → restart_backend() with no confirmation (runtime_settings.py:340-341). The button is the same size and weight as Apply. 'Applied: allocator cuda_async, torch.compile off.' (255-258) describes the saved file, not the running process. The 'Restart the backend for the new allocator to take effect' hint appears only once, in Apply's reply (143-147), and is gone after a reload.
findings.principle: P14, P13, NN/g heuristic 5 (error prevention), ML-CK-3
findings.fix: At import, capture the process's PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF (which shep_launch.apply_allocator sets) and map it back to a preset through ALLOCATOR_PRESETS. Show persistent inline text under the allocator: 'Running: cuda_async · Saved: expandable. Restart needed.' Enable a small secondary 'Restart backend…' there, on by default only when saved ≠ running. Its click reveals a confirm row in the same gr.Column (CSS class toggle, not visible=): 'Restart now: every open page reconnects in a few seconds' [Restart] [Cancel]. This mirrors the drawer's from → to confirm.

findings.title: The torch.compile warning hides in a bare 'Details' accordion, and the badges use six hues with no shared meaning
findings.evidence: 12-settings.png. The 'Details ◀' accordion (runtime_settings.py:321-329) holds 'Experimental / benchmark-only — keep this off unless you are explicitly benchmarking it… HGT has been observed to run slower…'. Badge colours (app.py:165-170) span blue, green, orange, purple, red and slate. 'Restart required' is red although it is not an error. The 'Memory' badge repeats the 'Memory' heading. 'Speed' (#15803d) and 'Precision ⚠' (#b45309) sit at about 4.3:1 on their tints. The intro refers to a '🔄 Restart required' tag, but the tag has no 🔄 (runtime_settings.py:225 vs 286).
findings.fix: gr.Checkbox(info='Experimental: often slower for HGT on GB10; compare MRR with an eager run before trusting results.'). Rename the accordions 'Details: what each allocator does' and 'Details: GB10 and HGT caveats'. Replace the badge rows with one muted line of text: 'Takes effect: after a backend restart' / 'Takes effect: next training run'. Keep a single amber lozenge with ⚠ for 'Experimental', on the status tokens. Fix the 🔄 reference.

findings.title: Read-only viewers can edit the fields and are told to click a disabled button
findings.evidence: _refresh_restart_lock updates the interactivity of apply_btn and restart_btn only (runtime_settings.py:166-171). The allocator and torch_compile stay interactive. Their .change handler writes '● Unsaved changes — click Apply Settings to persist.' (343-347) whatever the request's access, even though Apply is disabled for that request.
findings.fix: Add allocator and torch_compile to lock_outputs and return gr.update(interactive=access.allowed) for them. Give _on_change a gr.Request: for a refused request, return 'Operator controls only: <D8 short reason>' instead of the unsaved prompt. Add a test that a non-loopback request renders the fields disabled and the refusal visible at ≥4.5:1.

findings.title: Left edges do not line up, and Options is a box inside the panel
findings.evidence: 01: the HPO terms and Patient ID labels and boxes run from x≈41 to 361. The Options box, MODEL IN USE and Run span x≈33-369 (#shep-dx-fields .block.padded {padding: 6px 8px}, diagnosis_panel.py:2357). Options is a bordered grey box (2362-2363) whose checkbox wraps under Top-K at x≈129, not under 'Options'. The card is a third surface (2376-2377), all in a 370px column.
findings.fix: Set #shep-dx-fields .block.padded { padding: 0 0 8px !important }, so every block starts at the column's 16px padding. Drop the Options border and background. findings.title: The device notice shows twice with the drawer open, banners are all caps, and 'synthetic' shows three times

audits.overall:
Verdict: keep the current design and make adjustments; it does not need a redesign. The structure matches the research.
- Navigation: two levels, with the four Research pages kept as horizontal tabs (P09: a side nav is warranted only above 5 items).
- Diagnosis: reads left to right, input → ranked list → details (DX-14). The served identity has one card plus a drawer (DX-09).
- Help: one shared help registry with toggletip behaviour already covers hover, focus, click-pin and Esc (P06).
- Constraints: everything is offline (G13), and refusals stay visible as text (P14, D8).

Most problems sit in a few shared places, so fixes spread to every page:
1. Theme tokens. Gradio's subdued grey (#9ca3af, 2.54:1) is still used for placeholders and for info= text, including the HGT/AMP refusal. Inputs have almost invisible borders (#f9fafb). Field labels are indigo chips. There are 4 sizes and 4 weights, and status colours are raw hex.
2. Text. Help bubbles run 90–190 words in plain paragraphs. Option and row labels are dot-joined chains. The same fact is repeated on one screen ('No model loaded' 4 times, the scores twice, the device line twice).
3. The bubble. It renders through textContent only, it is 360px wide, and its placement covers the element it explains.
4. Group labels. PREPARE/EVALUATE sit on the tabs' 44px line at about the same visual weight, so they read as tabs.

These are wording, CSS and markup changes inside the current layout. Estimate: about 2–3 days for the light adjustments.

A few changes are structural, about 3–5 more days, and none needs a new page layout or navigation model:
- Move the footer warning into a header chip, and optionally put the Research tabs into row 1 when it has room (together about 77px back for charts).
- Diagnosis table: 'Score' instead of 'Confidence', a k/N phenotype column, and an echo of which terms were recognised and used.
- Candidate details: labels before ids, Mode A/B replaced by plain-language key-value rows.
- Settings: a panel layout with fields before actions, a running-vs-saved allocator line, a restart confirmation, and fields disabled for read-only viewers.

Decisions for the owner:
- The 14px text floor (style.py:5, enforced by the head-CSS test) conflicts with the 11–12px overline that P08 proposes. Either allow an exception for overlines or use the inline 'Prepare:' option.
- The group-label and row-1 fixes rely on Gradio-internal selectors (.tab-wrapper, .tab-container, button[role=tab]). Pin them with a selector-inventory test. If such overrides keep growing over the next milestones, open the G14 decision (gr.HTML islands or a gr.Server frontend).

References I checked directly (the shared web-search budget ran out mid-task, so I fetched these known pages instead):
- Floating UI flip() fallbackPlacements, for the bubble placement order: https://floating-ui.com/docs/flip
- NN/g, 'Placeholders in Form Fields Are Harmful' (placeholders vanish on typing and have poor contrast): https://www.nngroup.com/articles/form-design-placeholders/
- GOV.UK text input, hint text as one short sentence under the label and no placeholders: https://design-system.service.gov.uk/components/text-input/

Gradio 6.30 theme variable names (--input-border-color, --input-placeholder-color, --block-info-text-color, --block-title-background-fill) are confirmed in the installed .venv bundle. The subdued-grey defaults come from .venv gradio/themes/base.py:1149, 1201 and 1669.

audits.overall:
The design is sound and needs adjustments, not a redesign. The skeleton already follows the patterns the research recommends. Training is a run bar over Parameters, which a Continue drawer replaces, beside a three-row run view with a 2×2 synced uPlot grid that scrolls inside its own row. Datasets is a table with a details panel. Both use 12-hex fingerprints with copy, element-scoped JS, vendored assets and a shared help registry. The problems are in content and styling, plus a tight vertical budget, and can be fixed within this layout.

Two findings are high and each takes under 2 hours. First, the Device 'auto' help says it falls back to CPU, while the trainer refuses without CUDA. On this host that default produces a refused run, and nothing on screen warns of it. Second, the Hits@K chart hides three series, and its legend tells dashed series apart by colour alone; one palette colour also fails 3:1 contrast.

The owner's own complaints are only partly solved:
- **Checkpoint options** are still dot-joined jargon ('Latest save · … · Trainer val MRR 0.2800').
- **Help texts** are still pipe-joined fragments, with must-know constraints and no bold.
- **Repetition:** the idle state is said three times, and the Run details repeat the run folder and the dataset fingerprint.
- **Charts** sit at a 140 px floor because three rows of small text (snapshot line, toolbar, the second run-bar row) and the footer take about 150 px.

Issues the owner has not raised:
- a lock icon on enabled buttons;
- in-page radios that copy the level-1 header switch's filled style;
- label chips that look like links;
- field borders at 1.27–1.52:1 contrast and 20 px 'i' targets;
- a bubble that covers its own field;
- HGT silently changing a setting inside a collapsed accordion;
- a sticky toolbar left inside the chart scroller;
- the Datasets 'read-only' wording colliding with the D8 role;
- verification-level manifest hashes shown on Datasets' first view.

Only three changes are structural, all within the page:
1. A one-row run bar, with Run name moved into Parameters and the snapshot merged into the run-view header. This plus the footer change gives the charts about 200 px each.
2. Continue Training and Cancel moved into the drawer footer.
3. The toolbar moved out of the scroller.

Optionally, the checkpoint dropdown can become a radio table. None of this needs new navigation or a framework change. G2's left nav is unnecessary for four pages (P09), and the G14 escape hatch is not triggered.

Suggested order:
1. The two high fixes and the light CSS/wording fixes: device, legend, lock, idle repetition, checkpoint labels, radios and labels, contrast, nav labels.
2. Help text rewrite plus the safe renderer.
3. The vertical-budget restructure.
4. The Continue drawer restructure.
5. Datasets details and table cleanup.

The implementation refs to follow are the digest's: Gradio info= (already used for AMP_HGT_REFUSAL), (label, value) tuples, uPlot setSeries and setSize via ResizeObserver, Trackio's plot grid, GOV.UK summary list, Carbon toggletip and data table, and the OWASP createElement renderer.

audits.overall:
I audited the Test and Models pages from the five screenshots, the text dumps and the cited source (test_page.py, models_page.py, model_list.py, renderers.py, help.py, style.py, plus training_console.py for comparison). Verdict: the design is sound and needs adjustments, not a redesign.

Why the structure holds up. Test is a left-to-right setup → run → result layout, and Models is a list with a details panel beside it, the way ClearML and MLflow do it. At wide sizes the main actions stay in view (Start, Cancel, Register, Load). Refusals are inline and persistent. Fingerprints are 12-hex with copy. Almost every problem lives in pure Python renderers that already have tests, so fixes are cheap and testable.

Why it still feels overloaded. Most of the overload comes from one habit: facts joined with ' · ' into run-on strings. That shows up in option labels, the version details, Relations, R10 and the Load note. Two more causes: the same identity repeated across panels (demo-test-1 4x, f6f7e5cab280 4x, dataset fingerprint 4x on Models), and prose where a key-value list or small table belongs.

Things the owner may not have noticed:
- Two report rows read identically, because the time is cut to the minute, and they show different registration states.
- The Result can come from another workspace than the one selected. Only a clipped path at the panel's bottom says so.
- The R10 leakage figures ('3 of 5 test diseases seen in training') are neutral prose.
- 'Other metrics' sorts Hits@100 before Hits@20.
- '1 checkpoints in 1 runs'.
- Lock icons on enabled buttons.
- role=list with button children.

Two structural moves are worth making:
- Give Test the same Run → Checkpoint pair Training already has. The helpers exist in training_console.py:1980-2160 and should move to renderers.py.
- Move the Reports list into the Result column.

Everything else is wording, CSS or markup inside the current layout. The most useful shared piece is one key-value renderer for records, models and cohort versions, used by Test, Models and Training. The help bubble also needs a renderer for bold lead lines and bullet lists, built with createElement and textContent.

Constraint to flag: several texts are governed constants that must not be reworded without the owner's sign-off (caveats.py 'none rewords them', the D3 label, the §4.9 note). The R10 table and the tiered independence notice change how those texts are rendered, so the owner has to approve.

Rough effort: about 4-6 working days for all findings. The four high findings take about 2-3 days.

Implementation references: the in-repo precedents are Training's _run_choices/_checkpoint_choices/parent_details_html, models_page._metric_order, renderers.kv_cells, and the focus rule at style.py:321. External ones from the research digest: GOV.UK Summary list, Carbon single-select data table and Toggletip, the OWASP textContent rules, and Gradio 6.30's Dropdown (label, value) tuples with .change cascades and info= updates.

principles.rule: Each screen uses at most 3 text sizes, 2 weights (400/600) and 3 text contrast tiers (text, text-2, muted). At most 2 large elements per page, and the primary one is the largest. Proposed desktop tokens: 20px page/section title, 15px body/values, 13px keys/meta.
principles.why: Every element competing for emphasis produces overload. NN/g: 'If everything is contrasted, then nothing stands out'. Carbon's productive set uses 3 weights, with semibold for headers only.
principles.how: List every font-size and weight in style.py and components/*.py and map each one onto the 3-size scale. Squint test: blur a 1850x960 screenshot of every page by 5–10px. Pass if the intended primary region (ranked results, chart grid, table) is the dominant block and no more than 3 text tiers are distinguishable.

principles.rule: Each fact (model name, run time, epoch, checkpoint file, fingerprint, status) appears once per screen, in one canonical place: a short identity in the one-line header, values in the summary list, the full provenance chain in Details. A second appearance must add something (a delta or a comparison) or be removed. A body never opens by restating the header.
principles.why: NN/g #8: 'Every extra unit of information ... competes with the relevant units'. Redundant elements 'slow users down'. GOV.UK: 'Do not repeat the summary in the first paragraph.' Traceability is kept because Details still holds the full chain.
principles.how: Playwright test per page at 1850x960: collect innerText outside [data-details] and the copy buttons, then count occurrences of each 12-hex fingerprint, checkpoint filename and run timestamp. Fail if any appears more than once without an allow-list entry and a reason.

principles.rule: The first view holds what most users need for the task. Everything else sits one click away behind a control with a specific label (e.g. 'Details: run, checkpoint, fingerprints'), never a bare 'More'. Two levels at most: no popover inside a popover and no accordion inside a drawer. Never hide what most users need or what they must know to act (refusals, required inputs, units).
principles.why: NN/g: more than 2 levels 'typically have low usability', and the reveal control needs strong information scent. GOV.UK details is for information 'only some users will need'. NN/g complex apps: reduce clutter without reducing capability.
principles.how: Write a per-page disclosure inventory (Training: tab, then run view, then Parameters/Continue drawer). Pass if no fact needs two nested disclosures. For a single low-priority section use native <details>/<summary> inside gr.HTML; use gr.Accordion only for multiple sections.

principles.rule: Every label, option, chip, heading and help lead line starts with the distinguishing word(s), so the first 2 words (about 11 characters) carry the meaning. Sentences up to 20 words (hard limit 25). Paragraphs up to 3 sentences. Explain each technical term at first use. Use the active voice.
principles.why: Users see about 2 words of a list item, and 35% of links failed at 11 characters. GOV.UK: split sentences over 25 words; specialists prefer plain English too. NHS: up to 20 words per sentence, 3 sentences per paragraph.
principles.how: Add a unit test over the help registry and the option-label builders: words per sentence ≤25 (warn above 20), ≤3 sentences per paragraph, lead line ≤90 characters, no label starting with a constant prefix shared by all siblings. For example, write 'Epoch 2 · best val', not 'GAT · run 2026-10-24 …', when every option shares 'GAT'.

principles.rule: Any text longer than 2 lines gets structure: a bold lead line with the answer first, then bullets or key–value rows. Key terms are marked by weight, not by color alone. Panels use descriptive sentence-case subheadings with the key point first.
principles.why: The layer-cake pattern (headings) is 'by far the most effective' scanning pattern. The spotted pattern depends on bold keywords. Walls of text go unread.
principles.how: Pass if no visible paragraph runs past 3 lines at 1850px without a heading, bullet or key–value break. Help texts follow the grammar in P07.

principles.rule: The 'i' bubble behaves as a toggletip. It opens on click, Enter or Space and also on hover or focus. Esc closes it without moving focus, the pointer can move into it, and it stays until dismissed. Width up to about 320px. Body up to about 60 words or 6 lines, and only the body scrolls. Never covers the field it explains. Nothing needed to complete the task lives only in a bubble: that goes in inline helper text under the label.
principles.why: NN/g: 'Users shouldn't need to find a tooltip in order to complete their task'; 'lengthy content is no longer a tip'. Carbon: tooltips must not hold essential instructions; toggletips are at most 288px with body-only scroll. WCAG 1.4.13: dismissible, hoverable, persistent.
principles.how: help.py already handles hover, focus, click-pin, Esc and outside clicks. Add a test that enforces the word and line budget and sets max-width:320px. Move must-know sentences (units, formats, D8 refusals) into Gradio info= (6.30 renders markdown/HTML there) or into panel text. Placement must not overlap the trigger's field.

principles.rule:
Bubbles may contain emphasis and lists, built only with createElement plus textContent from a restricted line grammar: line 1 becomes a

lead; lines starting '- ' become

  • ; 'Term: text' becomes Term plus the text; a blank line starts a new paragraph. Never use innerHTML.
principles.why: OWASP: textContent is 'the most fundamental safe way', and createElement/appendChild are safe. This solves 'no bold, no lists' while keeping the existing contract that help text is never parsed as HTML.
principles.how:
Replace the bubble's `.textContent = textOf(btn)` in help.py with a ~30-line renderer and keep white-space: normal inside the list items. Regression test: a help text containing '' renders as literal text, and '- a\n- b' renders as 2
  • .

principles.rule: Non-interactive group labels (PREPARE, EVALUATE) share no tab treatment. (a) Size ≤12px against 15px tabs, uppercase with .06–.08em letter-spacing, muted color that still meets 4.5:1. (b) Not on the tabs' line or inside their 44px box: either stacked above the group's first tab as an overline, or inline after a 1px vertical divider with a gap of 16px or more. (c) No padding box, background, border, underline, hover or active state, or cursor:pointer, and pointer-events:none. (d) Not focusable, and never a separate element inside role=tablist. (e) The selected tab keeps at least 2 indicators (color, 3px underline, weight 700).
principles.why: NN/g: don't make non-clickable items look like buttons, and avoid things that look clickable but aren't; weak cues cause click uncertainty. NN/g tabs: tab labels avoid ALL CAPS, so small caps mark non-tabs. PatternFly: 'non-interactive group header'. Primer: group titles are headings with dividers. APG/MDN: a tablist holds tabs and is labelled as a whole.
principles.how: Current style.py lines 143-155 set the labels at 14px/600 caps, vertically centred in the same 44px row as 15px/500 tabs. Only 1px separates them, so they read as tabs. Change them to 11–12px. Either make them overlines (`::before{top:auto;bottom:calc(100% - 4px);left:0;right:auto}` on the first tab of each group, with the nav row about 14px taller) or keep them inline at 12px with a 24px gap and the divider. Checks: hovering a label changes nothing; the cursor stays default; Tab skips it; axe aria-required-children passes; the tablist keeps aria-label RESEARCH_TABLIST_LABEL.

principles.rule: Each navigation level has its own look and never mixes with in-page controls. Level 1 is the header switch (Diagnosis/Research), level 2 the page tabs (underline), level 3 the in-page segmented controls (contained). One row per control, labels of 1–2 words, the most-used tab first and selected by default. Keep four Research pages as horizontal tabs: a side nav is warranted only above 5 items.
principles.why: NN/g: 'Mixing in-page and navigation tabs within one tab control will disorient users'; make the kinds distinct. Material 3 has primary vs secondary tabs. Carbon uses a left panel above 5 items and at most 2 tiers. PatternFly uses horizontal navigation below 5 items.
principles.how: Screenshot review: the header switch, the page tabs and .shep-seg must differ in shape and surface. If both L1 and L3 are pill-segmented, restyle one of them. Pass if no two levels share one treatment.

principles.rule: Show the details of a single entity (model, run, checkpoint, dataset, cohort) as key–value summary lists. Markup: <dl>. Layout: a fixed key column of 8–12em (13px, muted), a value column (15px), an optional action column (Copy). 1px row separators, one fact per row. Sections (Identity / Training / Provenance) hold about 8 rows or fewer. Missing values show 'Not recorded' with a reason. Use a table only to compare several entities.
principles.why: GOV.UK summary list: key facts in a dl, not tabular data, and row borders help magnifier users. Carbon structured list: simple read-only data, condensed size available. PatternFly description list for detail pages. NN/g: tables are for comparison.
principles.how: Use one shared Python renderer, `dl.shep-sl` with `grid-template-columns:minmax(8em,12em) 1fr auto`. Term help, where needed, is a dotted-underline toggletip on the key (PatternFly) rather than more 'i' icons. Unit-test the markup (dt and dd pairs) and the empty-value text.

principles.rule: A fingerprint shows as 12 hex characters in monospace, never wrapped, next to a copy button. The button is at least 24x24px, has the accessible name 'Copy full <kind> fingerprint' and shows a visible 'Copied' confirmation. The full 64-hex value appears only in Details. Any truncation keeps the full value available on hover and focus.
principles.why: Carbon code snippet: click to copy, 'Copied to clipboard' feedback, no multi-line inline snippets. Carbon tag: start/middle/end truncation with the full text on hover and focus, no wrapping. WCAG 2.5.8: 24px targets.
principles.how: Measure button.shep-copy and the 'i' and × buttons with getBoundingClientRect ≥24px or check the spacing exception. Test aria-label and the confirmation text.

principles.rule: Option labels stay at about 30–40 characters, start with the distinguishing value and carry no dot-joined metadata chains. The chosen item's metadata shows in a summary list beside the select. For hierarchical choices use cascading selects: the child stays empty or disabled until the parent is chosen and clears when the parent changes. Under 5 options use radio or segmented controls; above 15 use a filterable combobox. When users compare candidates on several attributes (epoch, val metric, size), use a single-select table with radio rows instead of a dropdown.
principles.why: Carbon dropdown: 'brief, accurate, and not descriptive'; avoid multi-line; ellipsis plus tooltip; combo box for long lists. NN/g: combobox beyond 15 options, radios under 5. Carbon data table supports single-select radio rows. Tables beat other layouts for comparison.
principles.how: Gradio 6.30 Dropdown accepts (label, value) tuples, so keep value as the full id and label short. It cannot group options or show two-line options (#2951/#2970/#5227 not planned). Cascade two Dropdowns with .change(), returning gr.update(choices=…, value=None, interactive=bool). Show checkpoint metadata in P10's summary list. For comparison, use gr.Dataframe with a .select() handler, or a gr.HTML listbox or radio table.

principles.rule: One status palette for the whole site. Every status is color plus icon or shape plus a text label: error red, serious warning orange, warning yellow, success green, info or in-progress blue, not started grey. Read-only chips ('Operator controls: on', 'GPU jobs: none') are non-interactive: no hover, no pointer cursor, no button shape, and no truncation of essential text. Clickable items (Settings) look like links or buttons.
principles.why: Carbon status indicators fix color meanings and require multiple cues plus a label. Atlassian lozenge: non-interactive, never color alone, and truncated text in an unfocusable element is invisible. WCAG 1.4.1.
principles.how: Define --shep-status-{error,serious,warn,ok,info,neutral} tokens and grep for raw status hex values outside them. Check that every status chip contains an icon or shape and a text label.

principles.rule: Refusals and environment warnings are persistent inline notifications, never auto-dismissed toasts. Place them at the top of the affected region or next to the disabled control, with icon, color, a short title and 1–2 sentences, and put longer text behind 'View details'. The 'Operator controls only' text stays visible to read-only browsers and meets 4.5:1 even when the control beside it is disabled.
principles.why: Carbon: inline notifications do not auto-dismiss, run 1–2 short sentences and at most 2 lines, and pair a color with an icon. WCAG 1.4.3 exempts inactive components but not the explanatory text next to them. This also keeps the D8 access rule.
principles.how: Reduce the footer's torch/CUDA/PyG warnings to one inline callout title, e.g. 'Environment: CUDA unavailable. Training is disabled.', with the per-package list in a Details popover. Test that the refusal text is rendered (not display:none) for non-operator requests and meets 4.5:1.

principles.rule: Every empty table or panel shows a short title, one sentence on why it is empty and what to do next, and at most one primary action. A permission-empty state says who can act ('Operator controls only. Ask the operator on the server machine.'). No dead ends.
principles.why: Carbon empty states cover the no data, user action and error/permission types, use plain language, include a no-permission example and avoid dead ends.
principles.how: List every empty branch in the datasets_page, models_page, test_page and diagnosis_panel renderers and assert each one returns a title, a next step and either 0 or 1 actions.

principles.rule: Each chart has a protected minimum plot height (proposal: 220px in a 960px-tall window). Lay charts out 2x2 at 1600px or wider and in 1 column below. When space runs short the chart region scrolls instead of compressing below the minimum. Lines meet 3:1 against the background. Series differ by more than color (dash or marker plus a labelled legend). Color never encodes magnitude.
principles.why: NN/g dashboards: at-a-glance view, lines for trends, color paired with shape, no color for magnitude. WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1 for chart lines and 1.4.1 forbids color-only meaning. uPlot docs: width/height include axes and ticks but not the legend or title, so the legend needs its own height budget.
principles.how: In shep_charts.js, run a ResizeObserver on each chart cell that calls u.setSize({width: cell.clientWidth, height: Math.max(MIN, cell.clientHeight - legend.offsetHeight)}), and use axis size:'auto'. Test at 1850x960, 1536x760 and 3840x2160: plot height ≥ MIN and x-axis labels inside the visible region.

principles.rule: No sticky or fixed bar may overlap chart axes, table rows or a focused control. Status lines get their own grid or flex row. If a sticky header cannot be avoided, the scroll container gets scroll-padding-top or -bottom equal to the bar's height.
principles.why: WCAG 2.4.11 names sticky headers and footers. F110 is the failure; C43 (scroll-padding) is the fix.
principles.how: Playwright at 1850x960 and 1536x760: Tab through the run view and table. For each focused element, check that its rect is not fully covered by any position:sticky/fixed element (elementFromPoint at its centre returns the element or a descendant). Check the last x-axis label in the same way.

principles.rule: Use one spacing scale (2/4/8/12/16/24/32/48px): 8px or less inside a group and 16–24px or more between groups. A heading sits closer to its content than to the previous group. One container level per region, with no box inside a box. Labels and values align on shared vertical lines.
principles.why: Carbon: 'Space can also be used to denote groups of associated information' without dividers. NN/g: headings close to their content, larger gaps between groups, containers used sparingly.
principles.how: Grep the CSS for px values not on the scale (e.g. the 84px/116px tab margins, 6px, 10px) and map them to tokens or justify them. Screenshot review for nested bordered panels.

principles.rule: Text contrast ≥4.5:1 (≥3:1 at 18pt, or 14pt bold). Component boundaries, focus rings, selected-tab indicators and chart lines ≥3:1. Every interactive element shows visible focus: no outline:none without a replacement. Targets ≥24x24 CSS px or spaced apart. No meaning by color alone.
principles.why: WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.3, 1.4.11, 2.4.7 (failure F78), 2.5.8 and 1.4.1. Muted grey at 12–13px, used for keys and group labels, is the usual failure.
principles.how: Run axe-core from a local copy (no CDN) in the existing probe, plus a contrast check of every muted token against panel backgrounds at 12–13px.

principles.rule: Tables (Datasets, Models): compact 32px rows (40px default) with a header row of the same height. Column titles of 1–2 words that wrap to 2 lines and then truncate with the full title on hover. A table title plus a one-line description. At most 5 toolbar actions. Supplementary attributes go to the selected-row details panel, not into extra columns.
principles.why: Carbon data table specifies the sizes, title rules, toolbar limit and side panel for cramped expanded content. NN/g: tables exist to find, compare, view and act.
principles.how: Check that every .shep-tbl uses the shared row-height token and has no more columns than fit at 1850px without horizontal scroll. Move the rest into the details panel's summary list (P10).

implementation_refs.problem: PREPARE/EVALUATE group labels read as tabs
implementation_refs.reference: PatternFly grouped nav ('non-interactive group header') and Primer NavList group headings (semantic heading plus a divider per group)
implementation_refs.notes: Keep gr.Tabs with one tablist and its existing aria-label. Do not insert DOM nodes into `.tab-container[role=tablist]`: only tabs belong there (MDN), and Gradio re-renders it. Keep the CSS generated content with empty alt text (`content:'Prepare' / ''`). Restyle it to 11–12px caps, either as an overline above the group's first tab (`::before{bottom:100%}`, nav row about 14px taller) or inline after a 1px divider with a 24px gap. No hover, pointer-events:none. Selectors `#shep-research-nav > .tab-wrapper > .tab-container > button[role=tab]` are Gradio-internal, so pin them with a DOM test for 6.30. Also check the labels when the window narrows.

implementation_refs.problem: Horizontal groups with visible group labels: desktop precedent
implementation_refs.reference: Windows ribbon: labelled groups, group label below and visually subordinate to the commands, separators between groups
implementation_refs.notes: Supports the overline/underline option: the label sits on a different line from the controls and is smaller. Seen in search results only.

implementation_refs.problem: Accessible structure for grouped tabs
implementation_refs.reference: WAI-ARIA APG Tabs and the MDN tablist role
implementation_refs.notes: One tablist labelled by aria-label (already 'Research pages: Prepare (Datasets, Training), Evaluate (Test, Models)'). Group names are conveyed by that label, not by extra focusable nodes. Gradio already supplies role=tab and aria-selected.

implementation_refs.problem: Key–value details panels (models, runs, checkpoints, datasets)
implementation_refs.reference: GOV.UK Summary list markup: dl > div.row > dt.key + dd.value + dd.actions, with no-border and card variants
implementation_refs.notes: Port it as about 20 lines of local CSS: grid with `minmax(8em,12em) 1fr auto` and 1px row borders. Emit it from one Python renderer into gr.HTML, escaping every value with html.escape (as the current renderers do). Use the card variant for 'Run' / 'Checkpoint' / 'Dataset' groups. Nothing external is needed.

implementation_refs.problem: Key–value lists that need term help and columns
implementation_refs.reference: PatternFly Description list (horizontal layout, columns, dotted-underline popovers on terms)
implementation_refs.notes: At 1850px wide, a 2-column horizontal description list halves the panel height. Term help uses the existing help.py bubble, attached to a dotted-underlined dt instead of another 'i' icon.

implementation_refs.problem: Help bubbles: rich but short and safe
implementation_refs.reference: Carbon Toggletip (≤288px; header/body/footer; only the body scrolls; Enter/Space/Esc) and the Inclusive Components toggletip (button plus role=status live region)
implementation_refs.notes: help.py already has a shared bubble with hover, focus, click-pin, Esc and outside-click. Add max-width:320px and a bold title row, and render the body through a createElement/textContent line grammar (OWASP-safe), not plain pre-line text. Keep aria-describedby on the field. Gradio 6.30 has no built-in tooltip (PR #13894 closed unmerged 2026-09-25), so the custom implementation stays.

implementation_refs.problem: Safe formatting inside the bubble without HTML parsing
implementation_refs.reference: OWASP DOM based XSS Prevention Cheat Sheet (textContent; createElement/appendChild)
implementation_refs.notes: Grammar: lead line becomes p>strong; '- ' becomes ul>li; 'Term: rest' becomes strong plus a text node. Every string goes in via textContent. A regression test proves markup in help text stays literal.

implementation_refs.problem: Bubble stacking and clipping inside Gradio containers
implementation_refs.reference: HTML Popover API (top layer; popover=auto/manual; Baseline 2025)
implementation_refs.notes: Optional: give the shared bubble the popover='manual' attribute and call showPopover() so it renders in the top layer above Gradio's overflow:hidden and z-index contexts. It is native, needs no CDN, and keeps the current JS positioning. Check the deployment browsers first, because Baseline 2025 is 'newly available'.

implementation_refs.problem: Essential guidance currently hidden in bubbles
implementation_refs.reference: Gradio info= (renders markdown/HTML in 6.30) used as Carbon-style helper text under the label
implementation_refs.notes: Confirmed in the installed .venv gradio 6.30.0 Dropdown docstring: 'info: … Supports markdown / HTML syntax.' Use it for one short must-know line (units, format, D8 status) and keep the 'i' bubble for optional detail.

implementation_refs.problem: Long dot-joined option labels in selects
implementation_refs.reference: Carbon Dropdown (brief options, single line, ellipsis plus tooltip, combo box for long lists) with a cascading Run → Checkpoint pair
implementation_refs.notes:
Gradio 6.30 Dropdown renders `
  • ✓ label
    • ` as text, with wrapping (.item word-break:break-word, after #7467). It has no groups or secondary text (#2951 → #2970 not planned; #5227 markdown not planned). So: short labels, value = full id; the child dropdown uses gr.update(choices, value=None, interactive=False) until the parent is set; metadata goes to the summary list next to it. filterable=True is the default for long lists.

implementation_refs.problem: Choosing a checkpoint when users must compare epochs and metrics
implementation_refs.reference: Carbon Data table single-select radio rows
implementation_refs.notes: Replace the checkpoint dropdown with a compact table (epoch, val metric, saved, fingerprint 12-hex) where clicking a row selects it. Build it with gr.Dataframe(interactive=False) and .select(evt: gr.SelectData), or with gr.HTML whose js_on_load calls trigger('select', {id}). Keep the row value equal to the full checkpoint id.

implementation_refs.problem: A custom grouped option list if a dropdown is still needed
implementation_refs.reference: WAI-ARIA APG Listbox with grouped options (listbox > group[aria-labelledby] > option, aria-activedescendant)
implementation_refs.notes: Implement it as a gr.HTML subclass. html_template uses Handlebars {{#each}} for the groups and options, with primary text plus a muted secondary span per option. js_on_load handles keys (arrows, Home/End, type-ahead) via event delegation (listeners attach once) and sets props.value, then trigger('change'). Escape all values on the Python side. Serve it locally, not through head/CDN.

implementation_refs.problem: Building custom widgets in Gradio 6.30 without a CDN
implementation_refs.reference: Gradio guide: Custom HTML components (html_template, css_template, js_on_load, props, trigger, watch, server_functions)
implementation_refs.notes: Verified in the installed 6.30 html.py: js_on_load gets element, props, trigger, watch, upload and server. Do not use head= for libraries; keep assets in src/webui/static. The guide warns that untrusted template input is an XSS risk, so html.escape all data.

implementation_refs.problem: Rich option content (future, native)
implementation_refs.reference: Chrome customizable select (appearance: base-select, Chrome 135+)
implementation_refs.notes: Not applicable to gr.Dropdown, which is a Svelte listbox and not a native select. Usable only inside a gr.HTML native <select> as progressive enhancement; other browsers show plain text options. A low-priority fallback reference.

implementation_refs.problem: Charts squeezed vertically
implementation_refs.reference: uPlot docs (width/height include plot, axes and ticks but not legend or title; setSize; axis size:'auto', demos/axis-autosize.html)
implementation_refs.notes: In shep_charts.js, run a ResizeObserver on each chart cell and call setSize with height = max(MIN_PLOT, cell height − legend height). Set the run view's chart region to overflow:auto with grid-auto-rows: minmax(MIN_PLOT+legend, 1fr), so it scrolls instead of shrinking.

implementation_refs.problem: Sticky status line covering chart axes
implementation_refs.reference: WCAG 2.4.11 technique C43 (scroll-padding) and failure F110
implementation_refs.notes: Preferred: the status line is its own row in the three-row run view (no position:sticky over the chart region). Otherwise set scroll-padding-bottom on the scroll container to the bar's height. Add a Playwright overlap check.

implementation_refs.problem: Status chips and notification styling
implementation_refs.reference: Carbon Status indicator pattern, Carbon Notification and Atlassian Lozenge
implementation_refs.notes: Use a single token map in style.py, with icon plus label always (inline SVG, local). Header chips stay read-only lozenges. Refusals are inline, persistent notifications near the disabled control (D8).

implementation_refs.problem: Empty and no-permission states
implementation_refs.reference: Carbon Empty states pattern
implementation_refs.notes: One shared Python helper empty_state(title, next_step, action=None) used by every table and panel renderer. The read-only variant names the operator as the one who can act.

research.caveats:
How these sources were reached:
- GitHub search through gh and the REST search endpoints is blocked in this session (403). Gradio issues and PRs were found with WebSearch restricted to github.com:
  - opened: #2951, #7467, PR #13894
  - status from search results only: #2970, #5227, #4278, PR #9521
- discuss.huggingface.co searches turned up nothing substantive on tooltips, grouped dropdowns or tab group labels, so no forum thread is cited.
- Material 3 pages render with JavaScript and came back empty when fetched. Material guidance comes from search snippets and from SAP's Fiori M3-derived page.
- The NN/g data-tables article and the Microsoft ribbon page were seen only in search results.
- The Carbon status-indicator page contradicts itself: it asks for at least 3 of color, shape, symbol and type in one place and at least 2 in another.
