Local checks against the installed .venv gradio 6.30.0:
- Dropdown accepts str or (label, value) choices.
- An option renders as `li[data-testid=dropdown-option][role=option]` with plain text, and option CSS sets word-break:break-word.
- The info= docstring says 'Supports markdown / HTML syntax'.
- gr.HTML has html_template, css_template, js_on_load and server_functions.
- These DOM selectors are Gradio-internal and can change in any upgrade, so pin them with DOM tests.

Repo observation: style.py lines 143-155 render PREPARE/EVALUATE at 14px/600 caps, centred in the same 44px row as 15px/500 tabs. That near-identical treatment is the likely cause of the confusion.

My numbers, not from any source:
- 12px labels
- 220px minimum plot height
- 320px bubble width (Carbon's figure is 288px)
- 60-word bubble budget
- 8–12em key column
- 30–40 character option labels (Carbon gives no number; NN/g's thresholds are option counts, not lengths)

Tune them against screenshots at 1850x960, 1536x760 and 4K. Small muted text must still meet 4.5:1.

Browser support:
- Popover API: Baseline 2025, newly available.
- Customizable select: Chrome 135+ only.
- CSS anchor positioning: I did not confirm support (MDN content was truncated), so keep the existing JS positioning.

GOV.UK and NHS write for the public. Their sentence limits are a ceiling here: clinicians and researchers are specialists, but both guides cite evidence that specialists also prefer plain English.

principles.rule: Non-interactive group labels (PREPARE/EVALUATE) must share no visual or hit-area treatment with tabs. Not inside a tab button's box. Not at the tab row's height or baseline. No tab padding, border, hover background, underline or cursor:pointer. Use smaller-weight caps text in the muted colour, with a vertical divider and at least 24px gap before each group. Not focusable, not announced as tabs; the tablist carries an aria-label that names the groups.
principles.why: In Tabs.svelte the 6.30 tablist renders only button[role=tab], so anything injected there is read as a tab. APG requires that a tablist hold tabs. Primer models groups as headings plus dividers, not as items. The owner reports that the current labels read as tabs: they are ::before generated content of the first tab of each group, on the same 44px row and at the same 14-15px size.
principles.how: Checkable: in DevTools, the label's box does not overlap any button[role=tab] rect. elementFromPoint at the label's centre is not a tab. Computed font-size/weight/colour differ from the tabs. No :hover style change. Tab key order holds only the tabs. In 6.30, either (a) keep the pseudo-element but place it on its own line above its group (font 12-13px if the owner relaxes the 14px floor, otherwise 14px at weight 600 in the muted colour, with letter-spacing), or (b) remove the second row and use a left nav with real group headings (see G2).

principles.rule: On landscape screens of about 960 CSS px height, spend width, not height, on navigation and selection. Keep at most one horizontal header row (about 44-48px). Put second-level page lists and run/model pickers in a left column that collapses to a rail of 40px or less. Never stack two tab rows above a chart page.
principles.why: Every horizontal row is taken from chart height, which is the owner's 'charts squeezed' complaint. Trackio, HF's own experiment dashboard, uses a single 44px navbar plus a 290px sidebar that collapses to a 40px rail. The transformers CI dashboard (Gradio) uses a 300px sidebar inside a 100vh frame.
principles.how: Checkable: at 1850x960 the Training run view's chart area is at least 620px tall with no page scroll, and only one header row exists. gr.Sidebar in 6.30 is position:fixed; top:0; height:100%, has no rail and overlays the header, so do not use it for page navigation (it can serve as a right-hand drawer for parameters/Continue, offset below the header by CSS). Build the left nav as gr.Column(scale=0, min_width=...) containing a gr.HTML list with <h3> group headings and buttons that call trigger(); a Python handler returns gr.Tabs(selected=page) to a gr.Tabs whose button row is hidden by CSS.

principles.rule: Each page is a grid frame: header and status rows are auto-height and in flow, the content row is minmax(0,1fr) and is the only element that scrolls. Status and summary lines are in-flow rows, never sticky or fixed overlays above charts. Every flex or grid child on the path to the scroller has min-height:0.
principles.why: A sticky status line covering chart axes is the owner's complaint. fill_height is reported broken through 6.15 (#12510), and the forum shows calc(100vh) attempts failing. Trackio (.metrics-page {overflow-y:auto; flex:1; min-height:0}) and the transformers CI dashboard (container 100vh with overflow hidden, inner panels overflow-y auto with min-height 0) both use explicit frame CSS. The 6.30 Row(height=...) docstring: 'If content exceeds the height, the row will scroll vertically.'
principles.how: Checkable: document.scrollingElement.scrollHeight equals innerHeight. Exactly one element per page has overflow-y:auto with scrollHeight greater than clientHeight. No element with position sticky or fixed intersects a chart canvas rect. If anchors scroll under a fixed header, add scroll-padding-top (#12977).

principles.rule: Charts get a fixed minimum plot height (Trackio uses 250px), at least 300px width per plot, at most 4 per row, an auto-fill grid, and a per-chart fullscreen. When the frame is short, the chart area scrolls; charts never shrink below the floor. Charts that share an x-axis share one zoom window.
principles.why: Trackio's LinePlot height is 250 outside fullscreen. Its grid is repeat(auto-fill, minmax(max(300px,(100%-3*16px)/4),1fr)). Its README documents shared xmin/xmax zoom, plots_per_row auto, smoothing and grouped accordions.
principles.how: Checkable: at 1850x960 and at 1280x720, every uPlot canvas is at least 250px high and at least 300px wide. Zooming one chart's x range updates the others. uPlot gets setSize from a ResizeObserver on its container, not from a window resize.

principles.rule: Dropdown option names are short plain-text identities: at most about 40 characters, unique, with the distinguishing token first (for example 'Oct 24 16:38 · GAT'). Never a dot-joined provenance string. Detail goes in the component's info line (updated on select) or in an adjacent key-value panel. Never in the option text, and never only in a tooltip.
principles.why:
In 6.30 each option renders as plain text choices[i][0] at the input's width with word-break, with no HTML or second line. The closed state shows the name in a single-line , so long names are cut off (#7467). Maintainers closed tooltip requests and prefer persistent info text (#4278). info= renders an escaped inline-markdown subset (**bold**, `code`, \n to
), so emphasis is possible there safely.
principles.how: Checkable: max option-name length is at most 40, no option contains more than 2 ' · ' separators, and fingerprints appear only in the info line or the details panel. In 6.30: return gr.update(info='**GAT** · epoch 2 · `55d7b5b89fa2`') from the .select handler.

principles.rule: Drive selection logic from Dropdown .select (which carries index and value) or .change, not .input, or make .input handlers idempotent. Do not push choices or value updates to a dropdown from timers unless the data changed (return gr.skip()). Keep dropdowns out of ancestors that have transform, filter, backdrop-filter, contain:layout|paint|strict|content, or content-visibility:auto.
principles.why: From the 6.30 source (not yet confirmed in a browser): an option pick calls on_input and then blur(), and handle_blur calls on_blur and on_input again. Index.svelte maps on_input to dispatch('input'). So one pick sends 'input' twice and a plain focus-out sends it once; #6712 is a 4.x precedent. Timer-driven updates disturbed open dropdowns before (#5314). The list is position:fixed (#12993), and MDN lists the ancestors that re-anchor fixed boxes. The repo wires .input on Dropdowns (test_page workspace/version/model, training_console dataset, model_list workspace).
principles.how: Checkable: in the browser, count backend calls per pick with a logging handler; the target is 1. Grep the webui for '.input(' on gr.Dropdown and expect zero, or idempotent guards. Grep the CSS for those properties on dropdown ancestors.

principles.rule: Treat the 6.30 options list as present in the DOM for 200ms after blur or selection. Tests and screenshots wait for it to detach, or finish its animations. Do not try to disable it with CSS animation or transition overrides.
principles.why: DropdownOptions uses transition:fly {duration:200, y:5}. Svelte 5 runs transitions through element.animate (WAAPI, fill:'forwards'), confirmed in Svelte's transitions.js and the compiled 6.30 bundle. CSS-based reduced-motion overrides (old Svelte advice) therefore have no effect, and Dropdown does not check prefers-reduced-motion (Sidebar does).
principles.how: Checkable: a test waits for the [role=listbox] node to detach, or runs document.querySelectorAll('.options').forEach(e => e.getAnimations().forEach(a => a.finish())) before asserting or capturing.

principles.rule: The help 'i' is a toggletip: it opens on click, closes on Esc, outside click or blur, holds brief supplementary text only (no links or buttons), and states the key fact in its first line. Rich text is allowed only through an escape-first whitelist renderer (**bold**, `code`, a line break, '- ' bullets), never innerHTML of raw text. Content that operators must not miss belongs on the page, not in a bubble.
principles.why: The Inclusive Components toggletip pattern: 'Don't rely on title attributes' and no interactive content. Gradio's own render_inline_markdown escapes HTML, then applies a small regex subset, a proven safe approach already shipped in 6.30. Maintainers reject hover tooltips for accessibility and mobile (#4278).
principles.how: Checkable: the bubble body has no element types beyond p, ul, li, strong and code. The first line is at most about 90 characters. Esc closes it and returns focus to the button. A test feeds '' and asserts it renders as text.

principles.rule: Do not add Gradio custom components for modals, tooltips, leaderboards or dropdowns. Build small widgets as gr.HTML (or gr.HTML subclasses) with css_template, js_on_load, trigger/watch and server_functions, using event delegation on element. Use native HTML (popover, dialog, details) for overlays.
principles.why: Every package checked requires gradio<6.0 on PyPI: gradio-modal 0.0.4, gradio-leaderboard 0.0.14, gradio-markdowntooltip, gradio-dropdownplus and gradio-textboxplus. Gradio 6 moved to Svelte 5, so 4.x/5.x builds also need rebuilding. gr.HTML in 6.30 has scoped CSS and server functions, needs no build step and works offline. js_on_load listeners are lost when the DOM is replaced (#13136), so delegate.
principles.how: Checkable: pip freeze has no gradio_* packages, and grep shows no innerHTML assignment of server data without escaping. In gr.HTML ${} templates, escape the data in Python, because templates are raw HTML.

principles.rule: Custom CSS and JS target only elem_id and elem_classes, Gradio's documented '<elem_id>-button' tab ids, and ARIA attributes (button[role=tab][aria-selected], [role=listbox]), plus a short, tested list of internal classes (.tab-wrapper, .tab-container, .right-tab-group). Keep a selector inventory test that fails when a Gradio upgrade removes one.
principles.why: The official guide warns that query selectors on Gradio's DOM are 'not guaranteed to work across Gradio versions'. The Tab docs document the -button suffix. Tabs.svelte (6.30) shows exactly which classes and roles exist.
principles.how: Checkable: a test renders the app headless and asserts that each selector in the inventory matches at least one node.

principles.rule: Use gr.Tabs(overflow_behavior='wrap') for application-level tabs (no hidden overflow menu), Tab(alignment='right') for utility destinations such as Settings, and Tab(height/max_height) or Row(height) for native per-panel scroll. Keep page navigation in gr.Tabs rather than demo.route/gr.Navbar.
principles.why: 'menu' mode renders visually hidden measuring duplicates and an icon-only overflow button (an a11y bug fixed in July 2026, #13635). Multipage apps 'do not support interactions between pages' and Navbar is a flat list without groups. Height and max_height on layouts landed in the 6.x wrap-up (#9192) and exist in the installed 6.30.
principles.how: Checkable: no .overflow-menu in the DOM. The Settings button sits inside .right-tab-group. Timers and shared State keep working across page switches.

principles.rule: When an option needs description, provenance or comparison, choose from a table or list with columns (name, key metrics, short fingerprint), not a dropdown. Use gr.Dataframe(interactive=False) with Styler or metadata display_value, show_search, pinned_columns, column_widths and wrap. Selection comes from .select (SelectData.index and row_value) and fills a details panel.
principles.why: Neither Dropdown nor Radio in 6.30 can show per-option descriptions. Dataframe styling works only when it is non-interactive. Installed SelectData exposes row_value. The gradio_leaderboard pattern (search columns, column chooser with cant_deselect, filters) shows how HF designed dense model tables.
principles.how: Checkable: Models, Datasets and Test pickers that show more than 2 attributes per item use a table. Clicking a row updates exactly one details panel, and the fingerprint has a copy control there.

principles.rule: Theme fonts are plain strings with local @font-face, or gr.themes.LocalFont. Never use gr.themes.GoogleFont. Any JS client (for example @gradio/client for a gr.Server frontend) is vendored locally, not taken from the guides' CDN snippet.
principles.why: The theming guide: GoogleFont 'will be loaded from Google Fonts'. The installed LocalFont emits @font-face pointing at static/fonts/ in the Gradio package. The server-mode guide's example loads @gradio/client from a CDN.
principles.how: Checkable: run the app with outbound network blocked and see zero failed requests in DevTools; grep shows no 'GoogleFont(' and no http(s) script or link URLs.

principles.rule: If grouped navigation, rich option lists and dense tables keep needing DOM-level CSS against Gradio internals, record a decision. Either keep gr.Blocks with gr.HTML islands, or move the UI to a custom frontend on gr.Server, which keeps the Python backend and API. Do not keep growing selector overrides indefinitely.
principles.why: HF's own flagship dashboards left gr.Blocks: Trackio uses Svelte 5 'Gradio-inspired' controls built from Gradio's component source, and the Open LLM Leaderboard uses React with TanStack Table. Gradio maintainers now close per-component feature requests, pointing to custom components or gr.Server (#10886, #4278).
principles.how: Checkable: count custom selectors that target Gradio-internal classes per release. If the count grows across two milestones, open the decision.

research.caveats:
1) I did not run the app in a browser. The Gradio 6.30 behaviour comes from the pinned tag's Svelte sources (raw.githubusercontent.com/gradio-app/gradio/gradio@6.30.0/...) and from installed signatures in /home/user/SHEPHERD-Advanced/.venv. The Dropdown double-'input' per pick and 'input' on every blur are inferred from source and need a browser check before code changes.
2) The GitHub API for gradio-app/gradio and gradio-app/trackio was denied in this session. I read those issues through their public web pages via a summarising fetcher, so the issue quotes are paraphrases of what the pages show.
3) Trackio was read from its main branch, not a pinned commit. Its 2025 blog describes a Gradio dashboard; the current README says Svelte 5. Both were true at different times.
4) The custom-components gallery page rendered 0 components (client-side), so compatibility is judged from PyPI metadata of 5 packages only. All of them pin gradio<6.0.
5) Whether container-type alone re-anchors position:fixed is not covered by MDN's list. The repo uses container-type:inline-size in training_console.py and contain:size in charts.py; neither is on MDN's list (contain:size is not layout/paint), but check in a browser if a dropdown sits inside them.
6) The repo notes, which I did not verify independently, say that 6.30 rewrites css= (prefixing selectors, dropping @supports/@container). That is why head <style> is recommended over css= here.
7) The 14px minimum text size the owner approved limits how far group labels can be visually demoted by size alone; weight, colour, placement and divider must carry the difference.
8) Line references to src/webui files reflect the working tree on 2026-10-25.

principles.rule: Each run, model or dataset is identified in three layers. (a) A short human label appears in titles, lists and select options. (b) The unique ID or fingerprint (12-hex short form) appears only in that object's detail key-value table, with an icon-only copy button. (c) The full hash and paths are reached through copy, not shown as text. Checks: on any screen, a given object's fingerprint string appears at most once. No dropdown option, page title or chart legend contains a hex run of 7 or more characters, a .pt filename or a path.
principles.why: W&B keeps the unique run ID in the URL and the 'Run path' field, while the non-unique human name goes in the workspace and the top of Overview. MLflow's run header renders only runDisplayName, and Run ID and Experiment ID sit in the Overview table inside a copyable box. Aim puts the Run Hash in the sidebar, and Neptune copies its ID from the 'Run information' menu. No tool repeats the ID in the header, option labels and body. This directly addresses the owner's long dot-joined option strings and repeated identity.
principles.how: Header: '<run label> · GAT' plus a status chip. The Details popover has one row, 'Model fingerprint 55d7b5b89fa2 [copy]'. Dropdown labels never carry a fingerprint or filename; the Gradio (label, value) tuple keeps the full key in the value. Exports and logs keep the full SHA-256 for provenance.

principles.rule: Visible run labels stay at or under about 24 characters, for example 'GAT · 10-24 16:38' or 'stop-02 · GAT · 10-24'. Longer text is truncated with an ellipsis (middle truncation for names that share a prefix), and the full text goes in the title attribute. Chips and tags have a max width of 160px (compact) or 300px (regular), with an ellipsis and a title tooltip. Check: no select option or table cell wraps to a second line at 1850px width.
principles.why: MLflow generates predicate-noun-number names capped at max_length=20. W&B ('glowing-shadows-8') and Trackio ('dainty-sunset-0') use the same short form. W&B truncates long run names in the middle by default. MLflow's AliasTag caps width at 160/300px with an ellipsis and the full value in title.
principles.how: run_words(): drop the year when it is the current year, and drop the architecture when the page already scopes it. Use CSS text-overflow:ellipsis for end truncation; middle truncation needs a small JS helper. Put title='<full name>' on every truncated element.

principles.rule: Choose a checkpoint in two steps: run, then checkpoint. Each checkpoint option leads with a role word from a fixed vocabulary ('latest', 'best <metric>', 'epoch N'), followed by at most one disambiguator. Per run, exactly one option carries 'latest' and at most one carries 'best'. When the same file holds both, show 'latest · best'. Checks: option labels are 40 characters or fewer, contain no filename, kind or fingerprint, and no two options read the same.
principles.why: W&B gives the newest version the 'latest' alias automatically, numbers versions v0..vN, allows each alias on one version only, and suggests a best_model alias. Lightning's WandbLogger sets aliases = ['latest','best'] if p == best_model_path else ['latest']. MLflow 3 logs checkpoints per step and ranks them by metric (search_logged_models order_by). MLflow aliases (@champion) are role words, not descriptions.
principles.how: Replace 'Latest save · 195 epochs completed' and 'Top-k save · 21 epochs completed · Trainer val MRR 0.2867' with 'latest · epoch 195' and 'best val MRR 0.287 · epoch 21'. 'Top-k save' is internal jargon; other files become 'epoch 14'. The kind, filename, end reason and fingerprint stay in parent_details_html under the select.

principles.rule: An alias such as best or latest is a mutable pointer. Wherever an alias is the chosen value, the detail table shows the immutable fingerprint it currently resolves to and the rule that defines the alias, for example 'best = highest Trainer val MRR among saved files'. Run records and exports store the fingerprint, never the alias alone. Check: every 'best' or 'latest' shown has a resolved fingerprint row and a 'defined by' row next to it.
principles.why: Tags are 'a volatile reference', while digests identify 'a specific version' and are used for repeatable deployments. W&B moves 'latest' each time a version is linked. MLflow reassigns aliases without changing consumers. Provenance therefore needs the digest, not the label.
principles.how: Test and Models details: 'Checkpoint: best (val MRR) → 55d7b5b89fa2 [copy]'. Ledger and report rows keep the full SHA-256.

principles.rule: Resume and new-run-from-checkpoint are separate actions with separate defaults. Resume (same settings) defaults to the run's latest file. Evaluate, or start a new run from a checkpoint, defaults to best. The action is named by what it does ('Resume from latest', 'New run from best'), not by a file name. Files that cannot resume (weights only) stay listed but disabled, with the reason given in details.
principles.why: Ultralytics: resume=True restores the model, optimizer, LR schedule and epoch counter from last.pt, while most next-round experiments 'are new runs that start from your last good model' (best.pt). W&B separates resume (same ID), fork (new run from a step) and rewind.
principles.how: In the Continue drawer the Checkpoint select preselects latest. The Test page model or checkpoint select preselects best. The button text reflects the selection.

principles.rule: Status is a chip with a text label, an icon or shape, and a tinted background, using a finite vocabulary mapped one-to-one to backend states. Animation (spinner) is used only for running. Crashed (heartbeat lost), failed (non-zero exit), killed or stopped, and paused are distinct states. Idle or no-action states (for example 'GPU jobs: none') are plain muted text, not colored chips. Checks: removing color still leaves each state readable, and every colored chip corresponds to something a user can act on or should watch.
principles.why: MLflow's RunViewStatusBox uses tinted tags with an icon and text: green for Finished, red for Failed and Killed, blue for Running and Scheduled, and a spinner only for running. W&B defines six states with exact meanings. Carbon requires at least two of color, shape and symbol, with color 'paired with text', and says to 'Avoid using status indicators when no user action is required.'
principles.how: Chip CSS: a ::before CSS shape glyph, a label, and token colors with dark-mode variants. Header chips: show 'GPU jobs: 1 running' as an active chip, and 'none' as muted text.

principles.rule: The 4 metric charts form a 2×2 grid when the chart area is at least about 1000px wide, and a single column below that. Each plot canvas is at least 220px tall, with width:height at most about 3:1. If the viewport cannot fit two rows at that minimum, the chart area scrolls (overflow-y:auto) instead of shrinking the charts. Check: at 1850×960 every chart canvas is 220px or taller, and none is wider than 3× its height.
principles.why: W&B sections default to 3 columns × 2 rows, and report panels default to w=8 of 24 columns and h=6. Trackio fits plots per row to the width (1 to 6), with min_width=400 in its Gradio version. Grafana uses 24 columns and 30px height units, with typical panels at h 8 to 9 (240 to 270px). Mature tools fix the column count and minimum size and scroll rather than squash. The owner flagged charts squeezed vertically.
principles.how: Chart container: display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(480px,1fr)); grid-auto-rows:minmax(220px,1fr). Run view row: minmax(0,1fr) with overflow:auto. The ResizeObserver then calls u.setSize, as shep_charts.js already does.

principles.rule: One set of chart controls serves the whole chart group: x-axis (epoch, step or time), smoothing and y-scale defaults sit in a single toolbar above the grid, not on each chart. The hover crosshair is synced across all charts, and x-zoom either syncs across charts or offers one 'reset zoom' for all. Checks: there are no per-chart x-axis or smoothing widgets, hovering one chart shows the same epoch line on all 4, and all charts share one x-range.
principles.why: W&B sets X axis, smoothing and outliers at workspace or section level for every panel (SectionPanelSettings x_axis default 'Step'). ClearML saves scalar display settings with 'Set as default'. Trackio shares xmin/xmax 'across all metrics plots' and propagates x_lim through plot.select. uPlot's cursor.sync is built for exactly this.
principles.how: shep_charts.js already syncs the cursor (sync key 'shep-'+key). Add x-scale propagation through a setScale hook so zoom applies to every chart in the group. Put the toolbar in the run view's header row.

principles.rule: Smoothing never hides raw data. The default is 0 (off). When it is above 0, the raw series is drawn at about 30% opacity in the same color behind the smoothed line, using a debiased EMA. The control shows its value. Check: with smoothing on, the raw points are still visible, and the first points are not pulled toward 0.
principles.why: W&B: 'the original unsmoothed data displays in the plot as a faint line in the background', with a debias term. W&B section defaults are smoothing_type 'none' and weight 0. Trackio draws raw at base color + '4D' (about 30% alpha) and smoothed in full color, with a slider where 0 means none. ClearML has a show-originals toggle.
principles.how: Compute the EMA client-side in shep_charts.js. Add one extra series per metric (stroke rgba with alpha 0.3) for the raw data. Persist the smoothing value per viewer (see ML-PS-1).

principles.rule: Nothing overlays the plot except the transient hover tooltip. The legend, status line and run bar sit in normal flow outside the canvas. No element with position: sticky or fixed may intersect any chart's axis area. Legend and series names are 2 words or fewer ('train loss', 'val MRR'). Check: the getBoundingClientRect of the status line or bar never intersects any .u-axis or .u-over rectangle, at any scroll position.
principles.why: uPlot's width and height cover only the plotting area, excluding the title and legend, so surrounding UI must be laid out by the container. TensorBoard puts crosshair values in the run selector, not over the chart. The owner reported a sticky status line covering the chart axes.
principles.how: Use a three-row run view: bar (auto), charts (minmax(0,1fr), overflow:auto), footer (auto). Remove sticky positioning inside the scrolling chart row. Keep legend: {show:false} with the custom tooltip, as now.

principles.rule: Run and model details are a 2-column key-value table in a fixed field order. Identity: name, then fingerprint with copy. Then status. Time: created, duration. Lineage: parent run, dataset, source. Results: summary metrics. Files last. The header line carries only name, status and actions, and repeats nothing else from the table. Check: no value appears in both the header and the table except the name.
principles.why: MLflow's Overview order is Created at, Created by, Experiment ID (copy), Status, Run ID (copy), Duration, Parent run, Datasets used, Tags, Source, Logged models, Registered models, and its header is runDisplayName plus actions. W&B's Overview has Name, State, Run path, start, runtime, host and command, with config and summary below. Aim's sidebar has Date, Duration, Hash and Tags.
principles.how: One gr.HTML table per Details popover and side panel (shep-kv), with a shared Python field-order helper so Training, Test and Models present details the same way.

principles.rule: Selecting a row in a list (Models, Datasets) opens details beside the list without navigating away. The list stays visible, at least as name and status, and its name column is pinned left with status next to it. Checks: after selecting a row, the list and the selected row highlight remain visible, and the name column does not scroll away horizontally.
principles.why: ClearML's info panel 'keeps the task table in view', and its compressed view shows 'only the task names and statuses'. Azure ML pins display name and metric columns. W&B shows pinned columns on the left, and Neptune keeps pinned columns visible and puts them in legends.
principles.how: Use gr.Dataframe(pinned_columns=1, max_height=..., show_search=...) with a .select event, or the existing custom HTML table with a sticky left first column.

principles.rule: Lineage is one linked row per relation (for example 'Source run: <run label>', 'Dataset: <label> · <fingerprint>'), not a restatement of the other object's description. Following the row shows that object's own details. Check: a model detail panel contains no run parameters or dataset statistics beyond the label, fingerprint and link.
principles.why: MLflow links each model version to the run that produced it, and its version page shows the 'source run'. Clicking the source run returns to the run page (Databricks). W&B uses a lineage graph rather than copying fields between objects.
principles.how: In Models details, the 'Trained by' row sets the Training run bar or opens the run details. The dataset row carries a fingerprint with copy.

principles.rule: Comparisons show one column per item, with a 'Differences only' toggle that defaults to on, and an optional pinned baseline that stays as the first column. Check: with two models selected, rows with equal values are hidden until the toggle is turned off.
principles.why: W&B's Run comparer 'Diff only' hides identical values. The MLflow UI pins runs to the top so a baseline stays visible during filtering.
principles.how: For a Models page compare: two selections produce an HTML key-value table filtered in Python, with a gr.Checkbox 'Differences only' set to True.

principles.rule: Every empty region states its cause, and each cause has its own text. First use: what will appear and how to create it. Waiting: the job is running and has no points yet. Filtered to zero: name the active filter and offer to clear it. Not recorded: this run did not log this metric. Error: the cause and the fix. Titles are short and positive, with at most one action. For read-only viewers the action is replaced by 'Operator controls only'. Check: no blank chart canvas or bare 'No data' text.
principles.why: Carbon's empty-state anatomy is title, body with the next step, and one action, and it defines no-data, user-action and error types. Trackio shows setup instructions when no project exists and '*Waiting for runs to appear...*' when projects exist. In Aim, tabs are empty 'if not tracked'.
principles.how: Add a placeholder block in the chart cells and in the table and details panels, driven by one Python helper that takes cause, title, body and action plus a D8 flag.

principles.rule: View settings (smoothing, x-axis, collapsed sections, chosen tab) persist per viewer in the browser and are reapplied on reload. They are never written into shared server state, so one viewer cannot change another's view. Check: after a reload the same smoothing and x-axis are shown, and a private window still renders with defaults.
principles.why: TensorBoard 2.6 keeps smoothing, tooltip sort and ignore-outliers in local storage across reloads. The TensorBoard README says important settings persist across sessions on the same origin. W&B persists pinned columns and sort per workspace.
principles.how: Use localStorage reads and writes wrapped in try/catch inside shep_charts.js, keyed per page. Fall back to defaults when storage is unavailable.

implementation_refs.problem: Dropdown options are long dot-joined strings
implementation_refs.reference: Gradio Dropdown (name, value) tuples plus info. W&B and Lightning latest/best aliases. MLflow 3 checkpoint ranking by step and metric.
implementation_refs.notes: Already in place: _choices() returns (label, key) tuples, and the key holds the full identity. Change only the labels. Run select: run_words() trimmed to 24 characters or fewer. Checkpoint select: role word first ('latest · epoch 195', 'best val MRR 0.287 · epoch 21', 'epoch 14'). Use info= for one line such as 'best = highest Trainer val MRR'. Options are plain text, so chips and bold are impossible inside them. gr.Dropdown has no per-option description; the community gradio_dropdownplus is a custom component that would ship its own frontend bundle (local, no CDN) at extra maintenance cost, so keep detail in the table under the select.

implementation_refs.problem: Choosing which checkpoint is 'best' and 'latest'
implementation_refs.reference: Lightning WandbLogger: aliases = ['latest','best'] if p == best_model_path else ['latest']. W&B: one version per alias.
implementation_refs.notes: Compute both server-side when listing a run's files. latest = the newest resumable save (last.pt). best = the readable file with the highest recorded Trainer validation metric, with ties broken by later epoch. Give each alias to exactly one file. Defaults: Continue preselects latest; the Test page preselects best. Keep the rule text ('best by Trainer val MRR') in the details table so the alias stays explainable.

implementation_refs.problem: Fingerprint shown in many places, with no consistent copy control
implementation_refs.reference: MLflow DetailsOverviewCopyableIdBox: an ellipsis span plus an icon-only copy button with flexShrink 0, used only in the Overview table
implementation_refs.notes: In Gradio, render 12hex

implementation_refs.problem: Alias and label chips in detail panels
implementation_refs.reference: MLflow AliasTag: '@ alias', max width 160px compact or 300px regular, ellipsis, title=value. W&B: orange chip for an alias, gray chip with a lock for a protected one.
implementation_refs.notes: Add a CSS class .shep-alias (inline-flex, max-width:160px, overflow:hidden, text-overflow:ellipsis, white-space:nowrap, token background) used in gr.HTML panels only. Text form in dropdowns is 'latest', 'best'. Do not invent 'protected' aliases; the D8 operator-only rule is shown as text, not as a chip.

implementation_refs.problem: Status chips look alike, or color carries the meaning
implementation_refs.reference: MLflow RunViewStatusBox: tinted background + icon + text, spinner only for RUNNING. Carbon status pattern.
implementation_refs.notes: Python maps backend states to {running, paused, finished, stopped, failed, crashed, pending}, each with a label and a CSS modifier. CSS draws the shape with ::before (circle, square, triangle) so meaning survives without color, and animates only .is-running. Colors go in :root tokens with dark-mode overrides. Header chips with nothing to act on ('GPU jobs: none') render as muted text.

implementation_refs.problem: 4 charts squeezed vertically, and the status line covers the axes
implementation_refs.reference: W&B section layout 3×2, panel w=8/24 h=6. Trackio plots_per_row auto, min_width 400. Grafana 30px height units. uPlot sizing excludes the legend.
implementation_refs.notes: Run view becomes a CSS grid with rows auto / minmax(0,1fr) / auto. The middle row is overflow-y:auto and holds a grid with grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(480px,1fr)) and grid-auto-rows:minmax(220px,1fr). At about 1850×960 that gives 2×2 charts of roughly 880×300px. Remove any sticky element inside the scroll row. The existing ResizeObserver plus setSize (shep_charts.js around lines 599 and 823) already resizes the plots. Add a test that checks the bounding-box intersection between the status line and .u-axis.

implementation_refs.problem: Shared x-axis and zoom across the 4 charts
implementation_refs.reference: uPlot sync-cursor demo: uPlot.sync(key), cursor.sync {key, setSeries:true, match}. Trackio shares x_lim across plots.
implementation_refs.notes: Cursor sync is already implemented. For zoom, add a hooks.setScale handler on the x scale that calls setScale('x', {min, max}) on the sibling instances, with a re-entrancy guard, plus one 'Reset zoom' button in the chart toolbar. uPlot stays a vendored local file (no CDN).

implementation_refs.problem: Smoothing without hiding raw data
implementation_refs.reference: Trackio get_color_mapping: raw series at base color + '4D' (about 30% alpha), smoothed series in full color. W&B: faint original line and debiased EMA.
implementation_refs.notes: In shep_charts.js, compute a debiased EMA per series client-side (ema_t = a*ema_{t-1} + (1-a)*x_t, divided by 1-a^t). When the slider is above 0, add a twin series with the raw stroke at alpha 0.3. The slider is a plain <input type=range> in the chart toolbar (element-scoped JS), default 0, persisted in localStorage inside try/catch, following TensorBoard 2.6.

implementation_refs.problem: Run and model details read as a wall of text, and identity repeats across header, popover and body
implementation_refs.reference: MLflow RunViewOverview field order. RunViewHeader shows only runDisplayName plus actions.
implementation_refs.notes: Add one Python helper kv_rows(obj) returning ordered (label, html) pairs: Name, Fingerprint (copy), Status, Created, Duration, Parent run, Dataset, Source, Summary metrics, Files. Training, Test and Models all use it in shep-kv tables. The one-line header shows label, status chip and actions. A test asserts the fingerprint occurs once in the rendered page HTML for that object.

implementation_refs.problem: Models and Datasets list plus details layout
implementation_refs.reference: ClearML info panel keeps the table, compressed to names and statuses. gr.Dataframe pinned_columns.
implementation_refs.notes: Keep the table at a fixed width beside the details panel. Pin the name column (gr.Dataframe(pinned_columns=1) or position:sticky;left:0 on the custom HTML table's first column) and put status next to it. Row select fills the details gr.HTML. With interactive=False, read-only viewers can still browse.

implementation_refs.problem: Comparing two models or checkpoints
implementation_refs.reference: W&B Run comparer 'Diff only'. MLflow pinned baseline runs.
implementation_refs.notes: Optional for the Models page: a multiselect of 2 to 3 models produces an HTML table with one column per model, filtered in Python to rows whose values differ while a gr.Checkbox('Differences only', value=True) is on. The first selection is the baseline column. The fingerprint row is always shown.

implementation_refs.problem: Empty and waiting states in charts and tables
implementation_refs.reference: Trackio main.py: setup instructions when no project vs '*Waiting for runs to appear...*'. Carbon empty-state anatomy.
implementation_refs.notes: One Python helper empty_state(cause, title, body, action, operator) renders a small block in place of a chart canvas or table body. The causes are first-use, waiting, filtered, not-recorded and error. When D8 marks the viewer read-only, the action is replaced by the visible 'Operator controls only' text.

implementation_refs.problem: Element-scoped JS in re-rendered gr.HTML (copy buttons, toolbar)
implementation_refs.reference: Gradio gr.HTML js_on_load (element, props, trigger, watch). The guide says listeners attach once, so delegate from a parent.
implementation_refs.notes: Gradio 6.30 gr.HTML provides js_on_load scoped to the component element, with no document-level listeners, matching the repo's rule. Use event delegation on the element for data-copy and toolbar controls. Use watch('value', ...) to re-apply persisted settings after Python updates. Load no external script; shep_charts.js and uPlot stay served locally.

research.caveats:
How the sources were reached:
- W&B docs: docs.wandb.ai now 301-redirects to docs.coreweave.com. The URLs above are the pages actually fetched. One W&B run-page URL (guides/app/pages/run-page) was gated, so I used models/runs/view-logged-runs instead.
- MLflow: the open-source docs do not describe how the run, alias and status UI looks. Those claims rest on the MLflow UI source files I fetched from GitHub master on 2026-10-25, so components may move between releases.
- Seen in search results but not fetched:
  - W&B Run comparer and Rewind pages.
  - TensorBoard 2.6.0 notes.
  - Neptune getting_id.
  - The Gradio gr.HTML guide (the direct fetch returned 404).
  - gradio_dropdownplus.
  - Comet registry pages (version strings plus stage tags; 'Register Model' button). Comet is therefore not used in any principle.
- Neptune: one search summary said its dashboard toolbar applies smoothing and axis settings to all charts, but the page I fetched did not contain that. I left that claim out.
- Unreachable or unverified:
  - Determined AI docs did not resolve (DNS).
  - No primary source gave TensorBoard's default smoothing value.

Numbers that are my derivations, not vendor specs:
- The pixel figures (220px minimum, 480px column minimum, 3:1 ratio) come from Grafana's 30px units, W&B's 24-column grid and 3×2 defaults, and Trackio's min_width 400. W&B does not document the pixel size of its grid units.
- The 24-character label limit extrapolates from MLflow's max_length=20 generator.

Gaps:
- No ML-tool source addresses the PREPARE/EVALUATE group-label problem. That belongs to the navigation and design-system research direction.
- The navigator.clipboard secure-context limit (LAN http) is general web-platform knowledge, not taken from these sources.

Mapping to the repo (read-only check):
- shep_charts.js already has cursor.sync, a ResizeObserver with setSize, and legend:{show:false}.
- training_console._choices already uses (label, key) tuples. The remaining work is the label wording (checkpoint_words still says 'Latest save' / 'Top-k save'), zoom sync, faint raw series, chart grid sizing and the single fingerprint row.

principles.rule: The ranked list shows only the decision-relevant facts per candidate, in this order: rank, disease name, one score (number plus thin bar), and 'k of N phenotypes annotated'. Everything else (component scores, evidence narrative, paths, genes) lives in the details panel or behind a disclosure. Check: at 1850x960 CSS px the first 10 rows are visible without scrolling, every cell is one line, and the table has no prose column.
principles.why: FDA's own wording: present the basis so as to avoid 'information overload, including prioritizing the most decision-relevant information and making additional detail available as appropriate'. Bates: if it does not fit on one screen, clinicians resist it. Isabel, LIRICAL and Exomiser all show the same compact list, with expansion for detail.
principles.how: Diagnosis table (diagnosis_panel.py ~L1300-1315): replace the 'Evidence' prose column with a 'Phenotypes k/N' column. Render the score as right-aligned tabular-nums plus a CSS bar. The table uses table-layout: fixed with text-overflow: ellipsis on the name, and the full name goes in a title attribute.

principles.rule: Echo the inputs exactly as used, with their knowns and unknowns. Every HPO id the user entered appears once, either as a resolved term ('Seizure HP:0001250') or in a separate 'Not used' list with a reason (unknown id, obsolete, not in the graph, duplicate removed). The count reads 'N terms used'. Check: the resolved and Not used lists together account for every parsed id, and the CSV and report carry the same split.
principles.why: FDA Criterion 4: inputs are 'clearly identified', and the output shows 'knowns/unknowns ... (e.g., missing, corrupted, or unexpected input data values)'. FDA's example 1 has the output say 'whether any expected input medical information ... was missing'. LIRICAL prints observed and excluded features plus an input-error list above its differential. The current UI ignores names and says only 'Recognised N entries'.
principles.how: Reuse _parse_hpo_ids and the API's dedupe count. Resolve labels server-side from the local ontology (src/ontology/loader.py; no hpo.jax.org call, no CDN). Render a chip row (escaped HTML) under the input and once at the top of the results. Unknown ids get an amber chip with the reason as a text suffix, not colour alone.

principles.rule: Put the label first and the identifier second everywhere a phenotype, disease, gene or graph node appears. The name is in body type; the CURIE follows in a smaller muted monospace, with copy. A bare id is allowed only when the name lookup failed, and it then reads 'HP:0001250 (name not in this ontology release)'. Check: no renderer emits {id} without a label.
principles.why: LIRICAL titles show disease name plus a CURIE link, Exomiser shows symbol plus identifier plus name, and the Phenopacket 'type' is an {id, label} pair. Clinicians judge plausibility from names, and ids alone defeat Criterion 4's expectation of information 'whose meaning ... understood by the intended HCP user'.
principles.how: phenotypes_html (~L1416) and paths_html (~L1426) currently print ids only; _node_display_name merely strips a prefix. Add one shared name lookup (ontology for HP:, KG node 'name' as stored by src/kg/builder.py for MONDO/genes) and one renderer term_html(id, label) used by the table, details, paths and chips.

principles.rule: 'Matching phenotypes' lists ALL query terms in two labelled groups: 'Annotated to this disease (k)' and 'Not annotated (N-k)'. If excluded terms are ever supported, a third group reads 'Excluded by you but annotated'. Match-type marks stay one character with a one-line legend; if a richer matcher is added, follow LIRICAL's E / Q<D / D<Q codes. Per-term contribution bars are shown only if the model actually provides contributions. Check: the group counts sum to N, and the existing caveat sentence is kept to one line.
principles.why: FDA: understanding 'how the logic was applied for the patient (e.g., matching of patient-level data to criteria...)' supports independent review. FDA example 32 fails Criterion 4 for not identifying what most closely matched. LIRICAL shows a blue/red bar per term; Isabel's '...' shows which terms matched and how well; Exomiser has a 'Top Phenotype Matches' tab. Showing the unmatched terms is the 'unknowns' half.
principles.how: The result already stores _query_phenotypes, so 'not annotated' is the query minus matching_phenotypes, computed in the renderer with no API change. Use two <ul> lists with group headings in a gr.HTML (plain_html). Put the counts in the segment label, which segment_choices already does.

principles.rule: Show one primary score, named for what it is, and show each number once per screen. An uncalibrated score is labelled 'Score', never 'Confidence' or 'Probability', and its help says it is relative to this list, not a probability of disease. Component scores (GNN, SP) appear in exactly one place, either the table or the details Evidence, not both. Format: fixed decimals (3, as Exomiser), tabular-nums, right-aligned. Check: on a result screen, each candidate's score text occurs once outside the identity drawer and exports.
principles.why: Isabel states its score 'is not the same as clinical probability'. LIRICAL calls it 'post-test probability' only because it is computed as one. High displayed confidence drives over-reliance and lowers accuracy (Rezaeian 2025), and confidence display barely helps calibrate trust (Bussone 2015). The owner flagged repetition: details_header_html (~L1356) repeats 'Confidence · GNN · SP' already in the row.
principles.how: Rename the table header and drop the repeated scores from the details header, which keeps '#rank name ID'. Keep confidence_label as a word only if it maps to a documented rule. Help text goes in the existing ⓘ bubble as plain text (fine for one sentence).

principles.rule: Keep the visible list short and the remainder collapsed. Top-K defaults to 10. If more are requested, rows after 10 sit under a collapsed 'More candidates (n)' disclosure in the same table panel. Check: the first render shows at most 10 rows; one click reveals the rest; Top-K stays at 20 or below.
principles.why: Riches 2016: list length is 'a key predictor' of retrieval, and long, low-relevance lists 'may increase uncertainty'. LIRICAL details only the top 10 and puts the rest in a hidden 'Low Post-Test Probability Results' table. Isabel defaults to top 10 with view-all.
principles.how: Use a native <details><summary> inside the results gr.HTML, with no JS and no visible= toggling. That avoids the Gradio 6.30 unmount/remount leak already documented in view_update.

principles.rule: Notices are non-interruptive by default and tiered by severity. Only states that invalidate or qualify the result (demo answer, result produced by a different model, identity unverifiable, no model loaded) get a full-width banner above the table: a bold one-line headline, one detail line and a 'Details ›' link. Everything else (device notice, matching caveat, field help) is muted inline text or an ⓘ. Nothing informational is a modal or a toast. D8 'Operator controls only' refusals stay as persistent inline text next to the disabled control. Check: a normal, valid result renders zero banner-class elements.
principles.why: AHRQ PSNet: tier by severity and make only severe alerts interruptive. The CMS/ONC tipsheet and Osheroff: favour non-interruptive formats, with interruptive warnings as the last resort. A permanently shown warning trains people to ignore the ones that matter.
principles.how: Keep IDENTITY_BANNERS (renderers.py) as the single banner vocabulary and give it one CSS class. Audit diagnosis_panel for any other bordered or coloured callouts and demote them to .shep-note.

principles.rule: Give the intended-use statement one fixed place on screen and repeat it only in exports. 'Not a certified medical device; decision support for a qualified clinician.' appears once per screen, in the results panel footer (visible at 1850x960 without scrolling), plus in every export and in Model Facts 'Uses'. Model Facts also states the intended user and patient population and that the use is not time-critical. It is never a banner and never repeated per panel. Check: the string occurs exactly once in the rendered Diagnosis DOM.
principles.why: FDA Criterion 4(a) asks for intended use, user and population in the software or labeling, and says time-critical uses do not qualify. LIRICAL puts its 'does not make a diagnosis itself' disclaimer once, in About. Repeating a static warning feeds alert fatigue (PSNet).
principles.how: The code already places NOT_A_MEDICAL_DEVICE in the footer once, so keep it there. Add the intended-user, population and not-time-critical line to the Model Facts 'Uses' block, not to the Diagnosis page.

principles.rule: On the result, provenance is one line; the full record is one click away and never repeated. The results header shows the status badge plus one monospace line: 'Model 55d7b5b89fa2 · Graph <12hex> · HPO <release>'. Each item copies on click, and the full digest is in the title attribute. The full identity table lives in the drawer, the equivalent of Exomiser's 'Settings' tab and LIRICAL's 'About'. A missing field reads 'Not recorded', never blank or hidden. When the served model changes after a result, the badge changes state. Check: outside the drawer, each fingerprint appears at most once on the Diagnosis screen, and every identity row has a value or 'Not recorded'.
principles.why: Exomiser keeps the run configuration in a separate Settings tab, and LIRICAL lists the HPO version and data paths in About with the tool version in the footer. FDA wants sources cited 'with the date or version'. The ONC rule requires indicating info 'not available for review'. The transparency principles call for 'timely notifications when the device is updated'. Model Facts requires version changes to be visible to users. Published evaluations cite exact model versions (DeepGestalt 19.1.7).
principles.how: The existing badge, identity drawer and copy_button already provide this. The fix is removal: delete repeated identity strings from the card, banners and details header so the one-line strip and the drawer are the only places. Add the HPO release to the strip if the served identity records it; if it does not, show 'HPO release: Not recorded' in the drawer.

principles.rule: Explanations run in three layers: a one-sentence summary, then structured facts, then the narrative collapsed. The Evidence view opens with the evidence label and a summary of at most 2 lines. Facts follow as a key-value list (for example: Evidence type = Direct links in the knowledge graph; Shortest link = 2 steps; Direct paths = 4; Supporting genes = FBN1, TGFBR2). The generated free-text explanation sits behind 'Full explanation'. Internal jargon is replaced in the UI: 'Mode A — Direct path evidence' becomes 'Direct links in the knowledge graph', and 'Mode B — Analogy-based' becomes 'Similar genes'. Check: no paragraph over 3 lines is visible by default in the details panel.
principles.why: Bussone: detailed explanations caused over-reliance and brief ones self-reliance, so lead short and keep detail available. The FDA and ONC texts require plain language, defined as clear, concise and well organised. Miller recommends concise language and extended information on request. Tonekaboni found clinicians prefer explanations that point at patient features over example-based ones.
principles.how: evidence_html (~L1373): replace the <h3> Mode titles with a <dl> using the existing key-value table style, and put the narrative from _format_full_explanation in a <details>. Bubbles stay plain text, which suits only short definitions.

principles.rule: Show paths as readable, typed chains, a few at a time. Each path is one line of node chips, for example '[Phenotype] Arachnodactyly → [Gene] FBN1 → [Disease] Marfan syndrome', with the edge relation on the arrow if known and ids muted or on hover. Show the 3 shortest paths by default and the rest under 'All n paths'. Check: the default view has at most 3 paths, every node has a name and a type, and nothing scrolls horizontally (chips wrap).
principles.why: TxGNN Explorer's path explanations, with an edge-threshold sparsity control, raised expert accuracy in a 12-person pilot against score-only output. FDA asks to show how the logic was applied to this patient. The current paths render as bare MONDO/HP ids, which a clinician cannot check.
principles.how: In paths_html, map node to (type, name) via the KG node table and sort by length. Render an <ol> of flex-wrap chip rows; put the overflow in a native <details>. Node type comes from the prefix (HP, MONDO, gene) and is shown as text, not only colour.

principles.rule: HPO entry is search-as-you-type over label, synonyms and id, producing removable chips, from a locally served ontology. After 2 or more characters, show at most 20 suggestions: label, then the matched synonym in muted text if the match came from a synonym, then the id. Enter or click adds a chip 'Label · HP:#######' with ×. Pasting ids or a mixed list still works and converts to chips. Show a term count. Optionally show parent and child terms for specificity. Add an Observed/Excluded toggle per chip only if the model consumes excluded terms; otherwise do not offer it. Check: typing 'seiz' lists Seizure HP:0001250 within 20 rows; pasting 'HP:0001250, HP:0001263' yields 2 named chips; no network call leaves the server.
principles.why: PhenoTips (predictive search with synonyms; observed and not-observed), SAMS (synonyms, tree browse, present/absent), PubCaseFinder (candidates, then parent/child), PheNominal (type-ahead from a local HPO copy, synonyms and super/subclasses in Details; 15 down to 5 minutes) and Doc2Hpo (per-term negation toggle, lookup to replace) converge on this pattern. Phenopacket uses 'excluded' only for features looked for and found absent. Bates: ask only for information you need.
principles.how: See the implementation refs: either gr.Dropdown(multiselect) with server-side key_up narrowing, or a gr.HTML combobox following the APG pattern. Keep the textarea route as 'Paste ids', and change its help text from 'Names ... are ignored' to describe the chip echo.

principles.rule: The basis of the method lives in Model Facts as structured HTML and is reachable from every result. Model Facts has a 'How this ranking is produced' block with fixed rows: general approach (for example, graph neural network over a biomedical knowledge graph plus shortest-path table); data relied upon (graph sources and versions; training patients, real or simulated, with counts); validation (cohort names, sizes, metric, with dates); known limitations and untested sub-populations; update or change history. Unknown rows read 'Not recorded'. Check: all five rows are present, and the results header links to it with one click.
principles.why: FDA Criterion 4(c)(i)–(iii) asks for exactly these items in plain language. Model Facts gives the one-page clinician format (Summary, Mechanism, Validation, Uses, Warnings). The ONC rule requires plain-language source attributes and a 'not available' indication. The help bubbles are plain textContent, so this does not belong in a bubble.
principles.how: Extend the existing Model Facts renderer (renderers.py, which already has 'Uses' and SYNTHETIC_FOR_TESTING) with the 5-row key-value block. Link it from the one-line provenance strip with 'About this model ›'.

principles.rule: Each fact appears in exactly one place per screen, and panels read left to right as input → list → details. The details header carries only '#rank name ID'. The model card carries identity; the results header carries the badge and one-line provenance; the footer carries the device notice and exports. Check: none of the strings for scores, fingerprints, the device notice or the query term list occurs twice in the Diagnosis DOM outside the drawer and exports. One exception: the query chips may appear both in the input and as the 'as used' echo, because the echo carries different information (dedupe and Not used).
principles.why: Miller: localise and group related information and use left-to-right mapping. Bates: little things matter, and fit on one screen. The owner's complaint is the same information repeated on one screen.
principles.how: Add a test that renders a fixture result and counts occurrences of each fingerprint and score string in the concatenated HTML outputs. That catches regressions cheaply, in the style of the existing renderer tests.

principles.rule: Verify the basis display with users, not only with tests. Before declaring the Diagnosis page done, have 3 to 5 clinicians or proxy users each answer, from the screen alone: why is #1 above #2, which of my terms were not used or not matched, and which model and knowledge release produced this. All three must be answerable without opening help bubbles.
principles.why: FDA: 'developers may need to perform usability testing to evaluate if their implementation meets Criterion 4'. The transparency principles call for human-centred design, which is iterative and validated.
principles.how: Run it as a manual checklist in the acceptance runbook, next to the screenshots step. It is not automated.

implementation_refs.problem: HPO autocomplete over the full ontology freezes or bloats the DOM if all terms are passed as Dropdown choices
implementation_refs.reference: Gradio frontend DropdownOptions.svelte and Multiselect.svelte (6.0.1); HF forum thread on capping shown values
implementation_refs.notes: DropdownOptions renders every filtered index as li.item, with no virtualization. Multiselect resets filtered_indices to ALL choices on focus. So never pass the whole HPO as choices. Start with choices=[] and narrow on the server (next ref). Verify against the installed 6.30 bundle (site-packages/gradio/templates), since the source read here is 6.0.1.

implementation_refs.problem: Server-side top-20 HPO suggestions inside a native Gradio multiselect (chips for free)
implementation_refs.reference: abidlabs/keyup Space (maintainer example) plus gr.KeyUpData docs plus gr.Dropdown docs
implementation_refs.notes: Use gr.Dropdown(multiselect=True, allow_custom_value=True, filterable=True, choices=[], elem_id='dx_hpo_terms'). Wire dd.key_up(suggest, inputs=dd, outputs=dd, show_progress='hidden'). suggest(selected, e: gr.KeyUpData) returns gr.update(choices=[(f'{label} · {hpo_id}', hpo_id) for currently selected] + top20(e.input_value)); keep the selected values inside choices so their chips keep their labels. Ignore e.key in arrow/Enter/Escape. Build the index once at startup from src/ontology/loader.py (label, synonyms, id; prefix and token match), with no network. Chips render as div.token (span plus div.token-remove), so style them with '#dx_hpo_terms .token'. Cost is one round trip per keystroke, so set a low concurrency_limit or debounce with trigger_mode='always_last'.

implementation_refs.problem: A fully controlled HPO combobox (show the matched synonym, Observed/Excluded toggle, parent/child links) without a CDN

Evidence quality: the FDA CDS guidance (Jan 29, 2026) was downloaded with curl and read in full; WebFetch got 401. The ONC DSI guide and the CMS tipsheet PDFs were read through text extraction. The 2016 human-factors guidance was seen only in search results. FDA 'Criterion 4' material is non-binding regulatory guidance, not legal advice. A research tool may not be in scope at all, but it is still the best public statement of what 'showing the basis' means.

Thin product coverage: I found no public, detailed documentation of the result screens of Face2Gene, Isabel DDx Companion (only the Isabel Pro blog), Mendelian (MendelScan returns reports to GPs, not an interactive UI) or Phenomizer (method only, from search summaries). PhenoTips' own docs were not reachable (403), so its points come from the RD-Connect GPAP docs and search-result slides. The UI points about these tools are therefore weaker than the LIRICAL and Exomiser points, which come from their actual report templates.

Small studies: the research cited is small or simulated (TxGNN pilot n=12; Bussone exploratory; Rezaeian n=28; Riches had very high heterogeneity). Treat it as direction, not proof.

Gradio caveats: the frontend source inspected is 6.0.1 (HF dataset gradio/frontend), not 6.30.0, and Gradio is not installed in this container. Check the Dropdown no-virtualization finding and the .token / .token-remove class names against the 6.30 bundle before relying on them. KeyUpData.input_value and .key are documented only by example. The per-keystroke key_up round trip needs a load check on the operator's machine.

principles.rule: Ship one project skill, .claude/skills/webui-review/SKILL.md (name equal to the folder name, lowercase-hyphen). The description opens with the use case: 'Audit or change the SHEPHERD Gradio WebUI: screenshots at the deployment viewports, geometry, duplicates, contrast, axe'. Keep the body to 150 lines or fewer, as a numbered workflow plus links. Checklists go in references/ (principles.md, vendored-vercel-rules.md, pinned commit), and executables in scripts/ (audit.py, run with --help first).
principles.why: Only name and description are loaded until the skill triggers. Body lines cost context on every turn once loaded. Scripts are 'executed, not loaded' and give deterministic results. Frontmatter keys outside the Agent Skills set break portability.
principles.how: Check: skills-ref validate passes. wc -l SKILL.md is 500 or fewer. Description is 1024 chars or fewer. Frontmatter uses only name, description and allowed-tools (for example Bash(python scripts/audit.py *)). Do not set disable-model-invocation on the read-only audit. Put baseline overwrite (--update) behind a separate manual-only skill with disable-model-invocation: true.

principles.rule: A UI change is done only when the agent has run scripts/audit.py on the changed pages and attached (a) the PNGs for each viewport and (b) the JSON or text report with zero new Blocker or High findings. A claim without evidence is not accepted. Reviews come from a fresh-context subagent, triaged Blocker/High/Medium/Nit, describing problems rather than prescriptions.
principles.why: Without a runnable check, 'looks done' is the only signal. The owner's repeated complaints (squeezed charts, covered axes) are measurable, so they should be caught by the script, not by the owner.
principles.how: Steps: identify the changed views, run audit.py --pages training,models --out artifacts/ui/<date>, open the PNGs, list differences, fix, re-run. Optional deterministic gate: a Stop hook running audit.py --changed-only. Report format: '<page>@<WxH> [Blocker] issue (evidence: file.png)' or 'file:line - issue'.

principles.rule: Screenshot and measure every page at a fixed matrix taken from the deployment, not generic widths: 1850x960 (primary, browser window), 1920x1080, 2560x1440 (4K at 150%), 1280x800 (narrow landscape) and 1080x1700 (rare portrait), with scale='css'. At every size: document scrollWidth must not exceed clientWidth (no page-level horizontal scroll), and nothing is clipped without an ellipsis or title.
principles.why: Community skills test at 1440/768/375 (OneRedOak) or 1280/768/375. Our users run landscape 1080p-4K, so mobile widths waste effort and miss the 960 px-tall case where charts get squeezed. Reflow exempts 2-D content such as tables and charts, so the narrow check is about page overflow, not full reflow.
principles.how: page.set_viewport_size(w,h). Wait for networkidle and stable boxes. page.screenshot(full_page=False, animations='disabled', caret='hide', scale='css', mask=[volatile locators]). Then assert page.evaluate('document.scrollingElement.scrollWidth <= document.scrollingElement.clientWidth'). The 4K CSS sizes assume OS scaling; adjust to the real machines.

principles.rule: No fixed or sticky element (header, status line, footer warnings, bubble when not opened by the user) may intersect any chart's plot or axis rectangle, or a focused control. Each chart canvas must be the topmost hit at sample points along its axes. Tabbing through each page must never leave the focused element fully hidden.
principles.why: The owner reported a sticky status line covering chart axes. WCAG 2.4.11 and F110 name sticky headers and footers as the failure, and Vercel's rule says overlays 'must not cover the focused element'.
principles.how: In page.evaluate: collect elements whose getComputedStyle(position) is fixed or sticky. For each chart (.u-wrap or the chart elem_id), check rect intersection (rect1.right < rect2.left etc.), then document.elementsFromPoint at the axis corners and the mid-bottom, asserting the first hit is inside the chart. Also press Tab N times, asserting the focused rect is not fully covered by any fixed rect. Fix with scroll-padding-bottom equal to the bar height (C43), or by making the bar part of layout flow.

principles.rule: At 1850x960 the Training run view shows all 4 charts without page scroll, each plot at least the owner-chosen minimum height (proposal: 200 CSS px for the plot area, axes excluded). Series lines have at least 3:1 contrast against the plot background. Number readouts use tabular-nums.
principles.why: 'Charts squeezed vertically' is a geometry fact that can be asserted. WCAG 1.4.11 requires 3:1 for 'each line in a graph'. Tabular numerals keep live values from jittering.
principles.how: Galen-style relational assertions in audit.py: for each canvas, getBoundingClientRect().height >= MIN, and its bottom <= innerHeight minus the sticky bar height. Compute line-colour contrast from the uPlot series stroke against the computed background (a WCAG relative-luminance helper in Python). Check getComputedStyle(el).fontVariantNumeric includes 'tabular-nums' on value cells.

principles.rule: Within one viewport, the same fact appears once. Each 12-hex fingerprint, model name or run id appears at most once in visible text, except entries on an explicit allowlist (for example a table row plus its selected-details panel). No label:value pair is repeated across header, card and drawer.
principles.why: The owner raised the same information repeated in several places. NN/g #8: 'Interfaces should not contain information that is irrelevant or rarely needed'. #4 (consistency) is broken when the same thing is worded two ways.
principles.how: In page.evaluate, walk the visible text nodes (checkVisibility() and an in-viewport rect), normalize whitespace, and regex /\b[0-9a-f]{12}\b/ plus known ids. Count occurrences and report each duplicate with its two DOM paths and the screenshot crop. Keep the allowlist in references/principles.md.

principles.rule: Dropdown and radio option labels are 40 characters or fewer and contain at most one ' · ' separator. The full provenance string (run, epoch, file, fingerprint) never appears as an option label: it lives in the details panel or table with copy buttons. Long text containers truncate with an ellipsis (min-width:0 on flex children) and expose the full value via title or details.
principles.why: Long dot-joined option strings were the owner's complaint. Gradio supports (name, value) tuples, so the label can be short while the value stays the full identifier. Vercel: 'anticipate short, average, and very long inputs'.
principles.how: Unit test (no browser): for every Dropdown and Radio built by the app factory, assert all(len(name) <= 40 and name.count(' · ') <= 1 for name, _ in choices). Browser check: scrollWidth > clientWidth on a label without text-overflow:ellipsis counts as a finding. Test with a fixture holding a 120-char run name.

principles.rule: PREPARE/EVALUATE group labels sit outside role=tablist (or label each tab group through aria-labelledby). They are not focusable, have cursor:default and no hover or active style change, no tab padding box, underline or border, and a visibly different size and weight from tabs. A divider or gap separates groups.
principles.why: APG: the tablist holds the tabs. Vercel: interactive states raise contrast on hover, so anything with tab-like styling reads as clickable. The frontend-design skill lists all-caps labels and 'unnecessary labels above content' as tells. The owner said the labels look like clickable tabs.
principles.how: audit.py: for each group-label locator, assert not el.closest('[role=tablist]') unless it is the aria-labelledby target. Assert tabIndex < 0 and cursor != 'pointer'. Hover it, then assert computed background, border and color are unchanged. Assert its font-size and padding-block differ from a [role=tab] by at least 2 px. Run axe nested-interactive and aria-required-children.

principles.rule: Help bubble text starts with a one-sentence answer, then 3 or fewer short paragraphs or bullets (proposal: 80 words or fewer in total) with at most 2 bold terms. There are no links or controls inside a hover tooltip. Anything vital, such as the D8 'Operator controls only' refusal, prerequisites or errors, is on screen, never only in a bubble.
principles.why: NN/g: 'Don't use tooltips for information that is vital to task completion' and 'Provide brief and helpful content'. Carbon: tooltips are 'not interactive', with 'succinct, directive text'. Primer: tooltips are a 'last resort'. Our bubble already pins on click and has a close button, which makes it a toggletip, so it should follow the toggletip rules.
principles.how: Unit test over HelpRegistry entries: word count 80 or fewer, first sentence 25 words or fewer, bold markers balanced and 2 or fewer. Browser check: every refusal string from D8 is visible (checkVisibility) for the read-only role without hovering.

principles.rule: Help text is never parsed as HTML in the browser. Bold comes only from a fixed '**term**' convention, turned into <strong> elements built from escaped text segments. An unbalanced marker is rejected at registration, and '\*\*' renders literally.
principles.why: OWASP: untrusted data 'should only be treated as displayable text', and createElement/appendChild is the safe way to build structure. MDN: innerHTML invokes the HTML parser and is an XSS sink. VS Code ships exactly this pattern ('**' to <b> via createElement). Gradio maintainers also avoid full Markdown in info text.
principles.how: See implementation_refs 'bold markup'. Tests: '' in help text appears as literal text; 'a **b** c' gives one b; 'a **b' raises at HelpRegistry._add; the bubble body contains no element except STRONG (assert via querySelectorAll(':not(strong)') in the body being empty).

principles.rule: Every audited page and state (drawer open, bubble open, read-only role) is scanned with axe using the tags wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and wcag22aa, with target-size enabled. Known violations are stored as fingerprints (rule id plus target selector) in a committed baseline. A new fingerprint fails the run. Refusal and disabled-state explanation text must pass color-contrast (4.5:1), even though inactive controls themselves are exempt.
principles.why: Axe finds a subset of problems mechanically, and Playwright says many can only be found manually, so keep a short manual keyboard pass. Fingerprints avoid brittle full-HTML snapshots. target-size is off by default.
principles.how: from axe_playwright_python.sync_playwright import Axe; r = Axe().run(page, options={'runOnly': {'type':'tag','values':[...]}, 'rules': {'target-size': {'enabled': True}}}). Compare r.generate_snapshot() lines against references/axe-baseline.txt. Scan after opening each state, since analyze() sees only the current DOM.

principles.rule: Screenshot baselines are per platform and browser, captured with animations disabled, caret hidden, the mouse moved off-page, and volatile regions masked (elapsed timers, timestamps, GPU chip, live chart canvases, fingerprints of demo data). Baselines change only by an explicit manual --update run whose diff a human reviews.
principles.why: Playwright: 'Browser rendering can vary based on the host OS, version, settings, hardware'. Masking and style injection remove volatility. Automatic baseline overwrite hides regressions.
principles.how: page.mouse.move(-1,-1); page.screenshot(animations='disabled', caret='hide', mask=[...], style='.shep-elapsed{visibility:hidden}'). Diff with pytest-playwright-visual assert_snapshot(threshold=0.1) or a Pillow diff. Store baselines under tests/ui_baselines/<platform>/. Capture the GB10 and dev machines separately.

principles.rule: The harness addresses UI only through elem_id, elem_classes or data-testid that the app sets, never Gradio-internal class names. Every network request during an audit must go to the local server's origin; any other host is a Blocker.
principles.why: Gradio warns that query selectors 'not guaranteed to work across Gradio versions'. Gradio's own testing repo targets data-testid. The no-CDN rule is cheap to assert in the same browser session.
principles.how: page.on('request', lambda r: offenders.append(r.url) if urlparse(r.url).netloc != base_netloc else None), then assert offenders is empty after each page. A unit test greps src/webui for selectors matching Gradio internals (for example '.svelte-') outside one adapter module.

principles.rule: Vendor a pinned subset of the Vercel rule file into references/ and keep only the rules that apply to a Gradio desktop tool: focus-visible, aria-label on icon buttons, aria-live for async status, ellipsis and long-content handling, tabular-nums, native select colours in dark mode, no 'transition: all', hover/focus contrast above rest, and 'Delay the first tooltip in a group'. Drop the Tailwind, mobile safe-area and Next.js items.
principles.why: The Vercel skill fetches rules at runtime, but we are offline. A focused list keeps the skill body small, which is the 'right altitude' advice.
principles.how: references/vercel-rules.md carries a header line naming the source commit SHA and date. audit.py maps each rule to an automated check or a 'manual' tag.

implementation_refs.problem: Minimal safe bold inside the plain-text help bubble (server-side variant, recommended)
implementation_refs.reference: VS Code formattedTextRenderer pattern plus OWASP rules, mapped onto src/webui/components/help.py
implementation_refs.notes: help.py already escapes every text into the hidden .shep-help-texts container (texts_html, line ~154, html.escape(entry.text)), and the bubble copies it with textContent (line ~268). Change one function in Python: parts = text.split('**'); reject len(parts) % 2 == 0 in HelpRegistry._add (fail fast, like _check_key); emit ''.join(html.escape(p) if i % 2 == 0 else '' + html.escape(p) + '' for i, p in enumerate(parts)). The browser never parses author text: only the fixed tag is literal, and every segment is escaped. In the head script replace bd.textContent = textOf(btn) with bd.replaceChildren(...Array.from(src.childNodes, n => n.cloneNode(true))), where src is the aria-describedby element. The accessible description then reads clean text without asterisks. white-space: pre-line still applies, and a CSS rule .shep-bubble-bd strong { font-weight: 600 } styles it. Verify that the Gradio 6.30 HTML component keeps (any sanitizer allows it). No CDN or new dependency.

implementation_refs.problem: Minimal safe bold, client-side variant (when text arrives at runtime, e.g. from an API)
implementation_refs.reference: VS Code renderFormattedText: tokenizer, then createTextNode/createElement('b'); backslash escapes; doubled markers
implementation_refs.notes: About 20 lines in the existing help head script: function renderEmph(el, s){ el.replaceChildren(); var bold=false, buf=''; for (var i=0;i made by createElement when bold. Only text nodes and createElement are used, which are the safe sinks in OWASP Guideline #3. This is the same idea as VS Code (MIT), which uses ; is preferable semantically. Test in Playwright by evaluating renderEmph on '' and asserting no IMG is created.

implementation_refs.reference: OWASP DOM based XSS Prevention Cheat Sheet; MDN textContent
implementation_refs.notes: Rule set for the skill's code-health step: textContent, createElement, appendChild and replaceChildren are allowed. innerHTML/outerHTML/insertAdjacentHTML are only for constant strings. setAttribute only for non-event attributes. A grep check in audit.py lists innerHTML uses in src/webui. Today shep_charts.js lines ~417 and ~502 (card.innerHTML = cardHtml(...), st.tip.innerHTML = rows.join('')) should be confirmed to carry only escaped or constant text.

implementation_refs.reference: Inclusive Components toggletip; Carbon tooltip/toggletip usage
implementation_refs.notes: Our shared bubble has role='tooltip' but pins on click and has a Close button, which is toggletip behaviour. implementation_refs.problem: Detecting the sticky status line covering chart axes, and focus obscured
implementation_refs.reference: MDN elementsFromPoint; Gleb Bahmutov overlap recipe; WCAG F110 and C43
implementation_refs.notes: page.evaluate JS: const fixed=[...document.querySelectorAll('body *')].filter(e=>/fixed|sticky/.test(getComputedStyle(e).position)); for each chart wrap c: r=c.getBoundingClientRect(); overlap = fixed.some(f=>{const q=f.getBoundingClientRect(); return !(q.right<r.left||r.right<q.left||q.bottom<r.top||r.bottom<q.top)}); plus hit = document.elementsFromPoint(r.left+4, r.bottom-4)[0]; ok = c.contains(hit). Use both tests, because elements with pointer-events:none do not take part in hit testing. Focus check: loop keyboard.press('Tab') and compare document.activeElement's rect against the fixed rects. Fix: html { scroll-padding-bottom: var(--status-h) } (C43), or put the bar in layout flow in the three-row grid.

research.caveats:
The search budget shared by all agents in this workflow ran out (200-call limit) after about 30 of my searches. Two community skills (garrytan gstack design-review, the full designer-skills repo) were seen only through a marketplace mirror or a search snippet, not their own repos. The owner can ask for a follow-up to search further.

Sources seen only in search results (not opened):
- tiny-marked (the fetch returned 403)
- pytest-playwright-visual (maintenance status unknown)
- the Lighthouse README
- the Vercel changelog
- Galen
- MDN Sanitizer API

Repo facts I checked:
- Playwright is not installed in the repo .venv, so the audit harness needs a new dev-only dependency plus a one-time Chromium download (or a wheelhouse and a copied browser). That is an owner decision.
- help.py escapes help texts server-side and copies them with textContent, so the server-side strong-only variant is a change of a few lines.
- shep_charts.js builds chart cards and the chart tooltip with innerHTML. I did not verify what flows into those strings.
- The shared help bubble has role='tooltip' yet a Close button and pin-on-click, which is toggletip behaviour per Carbon and Inclusive Components.

My own judgements, not quoted from sources:
- elementsFromPoint ignores elements with pointer-events:none, so pair it with rect intersection.
- The 4K-at-150% to 2560x1440 CSS mapping.
- The numeric thresholds: a 200 px plot height, 40-char option labels and 80-word bubbles are proposals for the owner, not from sources.

Conflicts with the community skills:
- Anthropic's frontend-design skill pushes distinctive, bold aesthetics for marketing-style pages. For this clinical/ML tool, reuse its process (plan, critique, screenshot, quality floor) and its warnings against decorative structure, not its boldness.
- Community design-review skills test mobile widths (375/768). Our deployment is landscape 1080p-4K, so use the deployment matrix.

Accessibility tooling limits:
- Automated axe and Lighthouse checks cover only part of WCAG. Playwright's docs say manual testing is still needed, so keep a short keyboard pass (Tab order, Esc closes the bubble, no fully hidden focus).
- Axe's target-size rule is disabled by default and must be enabled explicitly.

Gradio:
- Gradio's own repo has no Python screenshot-diff harness to borrow. Its browser tests are TypeScript Playwright specs plus Storybook.
- Gradio warns that custom selectors may break across versions, so the harness should rely only on app-set elem_id, elem_classes or data-testid.
